author: Greg Nammacher
title: How Minnesota Unions and Community Groups Stood Up to an ICE Occupation
content:
In this excerpt from the new book

This Is How We Win: A Guide to Building Working-Class Uprisings

, SEIU Local 26 President Greg Nammacher describes how his union, its members battered and exhausted from ICE attacks, went on the offensive against a federal occupation of Minnesota. -Editors


Trump’s Operation Metro Surge was a direct attack on our union. We represent 8,000 property service workers, security guards, janitors, airport workers, and Uber/Lyft drivers in the Twin Cities metro area, and the vast majority of our members are immigrants and people of color. Thirty of our members were abducted by ICE during the onslaught. Rideshare drivers had their windows smashed and were dragged through them by agents who detained them, their cars abandoned on the road behind the airport. Other airport workers, despite having badges indicating full background checks, were repeatedly stopped and harassed for no apparent reason other than that they looked East African. Latino members were stuck in the stores where they work, in some cases for hours on end, as ICE agents circled outside.


It was clear that our union had to do everything possible to support our members in this time of incredible fear and pressure. During the first month, we focused on mutual aid. We helped put together a support system of community volunteers to give members who were afraid to leave the house a ride to work, many in the middle of the night. We pushed employers to let people take leaves of absence or change their shifts. To be clear, people weren’t staying home because of their work or immigration status. They were staying home because we could see that federal agents were stopping and arresting people because of their skin color or accent, regardless of status.


Though we were still on the defensive, we were able to organize two public actions on December 3 and 20. In both cases, we were concerned that ICE would attack us. But people’s courage prevailed. ICE didn’t come, and we got valuable information about how fed up the public was. We learned that members of other unions and community organizations were morally outraged by the invasion. The belligerent ICE presence had made people more willing to speak up for themselves and their neighbors.


By the new year, the work of providing services and mutual aid had started to exhaust us. When ICE murdered Renée Good, it was a wake-up call that we can’t service our way out of an authoritarian occupation of our city. We had to go on offense—create some real pressure on those who were making the decision to occupy our city.


This Is How We Win: A Guide to Building Working-Class Uprisings,

 edited by Sarah Lazare and Amie Stager, is available from Haymarket Books.


When community and faith groups first made the call in early to mid-January for a day of “no work, no school, no shopping,” we held an emergency meeting of our stewards. It was conducted over Zoom, because people were so afraid to leave their own homes. But 95 percent of the folks on that call said clearly that they planned to not go to work on the day of economic shutdown. It was a measure of how sick and tired everybody was. Plus the December protests boosted our confidence that others in the Twin Cities would join the call.


How did we get to that spot, where members were willing to take action together? In our union’s contract fights for the last decade, we’ve prepared ourselves and gone on strike many times. Members and stewards know that in the United States, withholding our labor is a key part of our power as workers. Obviously we go to the ballot box. Obviously we hold our politicians accountable by pressuring them. We try everything that we can to advance a workers’ agenda. But the best way to get results in a fight with the boss is to withhold our labor. And so, having practiced that, people had that muscle when the moment came.


We had also done internal work in coalition with others to sharpen our analysis of how the Trump administration, through its federal occupations, was implementing a playbook that we’ve seen many times around the world from wannabe dictators. Many of our immigrant members have seen firsthand what happened in their home countries when dictators took over, and it wasn’t pretty. And we know the way to beat these authoritarian, power-hungry types: with large-scale mobilizations that disrupt the status quo. Our stewards not only had the experience of organizing strikes, but they also had an analysis …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Toxic Nightmare": 25 Years After 9/11, Juan González on His Predictions of Worker Illness & Death
content:
Twenty-five years after September 11, 2001, more people are believed to have died from cancer, respiratory and other illnesses due to exposure to the airborne toxins than the nearly 3,000 people killed in the attacks on the World Trade Center. In the weeks and months that followed 9/11, former New York City Mayors Rudy Giuliani and Michael Bloomberg, as well as other city and federal officials, reassured residents and workers it was safe to return to the area surrounding ground zero, concealing the dangers of lingering toxins in the air after the collapse of the twin towers.


Democracy Now!

 co-host Juan González reads from his book,

Fallout

, in which he extensively reported on the toxic nightmare around ground zero. “No one could guarantee the air around Ground Zero was safe because no one had ever confronted a disaster of such proportions,” González wrote in

Fallout

.

author: Natascha Elena Uhlmann
title: Vermont Hospital Workers Are Building Solidarity With Farmworkers
content:
University of Vermont Medical Center’s health care workers want their employer to join the Milk with Dignity program.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Health care workers fighting for a contract in Vermont have come to the table with not only their own demands for safe staffing and fair pay, but also a more unusual demand — one made in solidarity with farmworkers.

They want their employer, the University of Vermont Medical Center, to join the Milk with Dignity program.

“We’ve been in spaces with folks, seen them, heard their stories. They’ve come to our rallies,” said administrative assistant Melissa Lavallee, secretary of the union, Support Staff United (AFT-VT). “We’re doing for our neighbors what they do for us.”

Milk with Dignity, a framework authored by farmworkers through the local organizing project Migrant Justice, requires affiliated farms to commit to a number of labor standards. It’s modeled off of the Fair Food Program developed by the Coalition of Immokalee Workers, which organizes tomato pickers in Florida.

Farmworkers receive better wages, paid sick time, protection from discipline should they stop performing a task that could put their safety and “serious and immediate danger,” and education on their rights under the agreement.

Migrant Justice notched a big win in 2017 when Ben & Jerry’s — which produces more than 500 pints of ice cream a day in its facility in St. Albans, Vermont — signed an agreement to source dairy from farms that comply with Milk With Dignity’s labor standards. Grocery chain Hannaford has faced years of pressure, but has yet to commit.

Farmworkers and advocates set their sights on the University of Vermont Medical Center for good reason: “Every day, UVM Medical Center serves thousands of patients and workers. It is undoubtedly one of the largest institutional sourcers of dairy in the state,” said Will Lambek, an organizer with Migrant Justice. “By joining Milk with Dignity, the hospital can play a leadership role, inspiring other institutions — including hospitals, schools, and universities — to follow suit,” he said.

Organizers tried to bring the medical center to the table around 2022, but were unsuccessful. “Migrant Justice did not on its own have enough power to take on this important step,” Lambek said. “That’s why it’s so important to have [hospital] workers as allies in this fight.”

“Some don’t understand: ‘What does a farmer’s working conditions have to do with us?’” Lavallee said. “I grew up on a farm in Vermont, and it is the hardest work. Their working conditions are creating our food. Why would we want food created in terrible conditions?”

Health care workers are stretched thinner than ever. Across the country, 52 hospitals and health systems have announced staffing cuts since January. Trump is adding fuel to the fire with his two-pronged assault: Medicaid cuts, and the revocation of work permits for immigrants from countries including Cuba, Haiti, Nicaragua, and Venezuela, many of whom work in health care.

Support Staff United members have been in bargaining for their second contract since April. Among their key priorities is a safe staffing pay differential, to be paid when staffing drops below 80 percent of what is scheduled. They also want to see more paid time off to recover from injuries sustained at work: “My co-workers have been punched in the face. They’ve had ribs fractured. They’ve had fingers broken,” LNA Saer McCillian told Vermont Business.

Brett Rhodes, a nursing assistant who is now the union’s vice president of organizing, first decided to organize in 2022 after seeing how different things seemed for nurses compared to nursing assistants.

“The nurses had a union. I didn’t really know much about it, I just knew they were getting more respect and more staff,” he said. “When they said something, it had more weight to it. It seemed like they could solve their problems.”

On a typical shift, a nursing assistant must monitor a patient’s heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate, and body temperature, reposition them to prevent bed sores, monitor their blood sugar and any changes to their mental state, and help them eat and drink. They also shuttle the patient to and from the bathroom safely, and if necessary, clean them up after a bowel movement.

Now try adding nine other patients to the mix. That’s the average load that …

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Uber Is Suddenly Sticking up for Workers’ Rights Now Robotaxis Are Here
content:
Uber has teamed up with labour unions in two US states to fight off competition from driverless car companies.


The company is working with unions in Washington and New Jersey, the Financial Times

reported

, as it pushes for “hybrid networks” that would require human drivers to be seated in robotaxis. 


The move comes as the race to expand autonomous cars intensifies. Uber has just launched 15 self-driving cars with British firm Wayve in London, giving it an early lead over future rivals. 


But in the US, Uber is facing competition from Google-owned Waymo, which operates robotaxis in

14 cities

. Self-driving cars can be hired on Uber in just four. 


New alliances between Uber and unions mark a departure for the ride-hailing tech firm, which spent years blocking attempts to unionise among its drivers. In

Seattle

, the company repeatedly challenged laws designed to give drivers collective bargaining rights. 


Following the implementation of new laws in California, Uber also spent

$59 million

 lobbying for its overturn so that it wouldn’t have to pay drivers the minimum wage. 


But with driverless cars threatening to cut Uber and its drivers out of the market, company president Andrew MacDonald says its approach to worker protections has “changed”. 


“Today, we partner with cities instead of confronting them,” he wrote on

LinkedIn

 in May. “We’ve struck dozens of deals with labour groups for worker protections, and we work alongside hundreds of thousands of taxi drivers around the world.”


He acknowledged that Uber’s newfound interest in protecting drivers “might feel ironic”.


Despite pushing for stronger regulations, Uber is still investing heavily in the emerging technology. Last week, Uber announced

3,000 job cuts

 to redirect funds towards investment in future opportunities, including robotaxis. 


Manny Pastreich, the president of US union 32BJ SEIU, told the Financial Times: “Where Uber for their own strategic reason is opposing deployments, we’ll take it. Am I going to depend on that? No. I’m not.”

author: Simon Childs
title: Tommy Robinson’s Right-Hand Man Is Turning Online Hate Into an Anti-Migrant Militia
content:
In Portsmouth on Sunday, a man accosted a police officer, saying: “You know who I am? My name’s Danny Tommo. You saw what we did in Dover, and if you don’t stop right now, I’m calling 1,000 men to come to this place.”


He then started to vomit, having run (by his own reckoning) about four breathless miles to get to the lifeboat station in Eastney, where a boat was offboarding a group of migrants who had been rescued at sea.


Live-streaming his adventure to an audience on YouTube, he jumped over fences, making up for a lack of athleticism with a wild-eyed sense of urgency and determination. “If we’re being sick by the time we get there, we’re being sick – let’s go,” he said, panting as he ran.


He encouraged both those he encountered in the street and those watching – “every man and his dog” – to join him. By the end of the night, around 200 people had gathered around the harbour, some wearing masks, confronting riot police in order to stop the arrival of 120 people who had been travelling to the UK in a single dinghy.


But who is this queasy, far-right Pied Piper?


Daniel Thomas, a man with a history of grim but farcical missteps. In 2016, he was

one of three men jailed

 for attempting to kidnap the wrong person at knifepoint, as they tried to retrieve £10,000. After he was released, he styled himself ‘Danny Tommo’ and became an associate of Tommy Robinson, real name Stephen Yaxley-Lennon. He is a born-again Christian and describes himself as a

“guardian of faith”

. In recent months, Tommo has gained prominence as an influencer in his own right – perhaps most memorably by angrily demanding answers from the police

over a crime that never happened

, in the process causing a riot in the usually tranquil commuter town of Epsom in Surrey.


Last year, Tommo attached himself to Raise the Colours – the activist group which erected union jack and St George’s Cross flags across the country – and its founder, Ryan Bridge. The pair became anti-migrant vigilantes in northern France, filming themselves slashing dinghies. They were

planning something called

 Operation Overlord (named in reference to D-Day in 1944, on which allied armies began liberating Nazi-occupied Europe), aiming to storm the channel with boats. But Tommo and Bridge then fell out in

a messy public spat

, accusing each other of chasing fame and throwing out unproven allegations of misusing donations.


The YouTube livestream from Portsmouth, which has nearly 700,000 views at the time of writing, is certainly a bizarre watch. At one moment, Tommo is on the shore shouting at the police about alleged sex crimes perpetrated by migrants. The next, he is wading into the water, warning police “I will drown myself if you come near me” – apparently about to fulfil anti-fascists’ long-held wish for the far right to “get in the sea”.


But while the stream is strange at times, it also shows how far-right figures are organising and the blurred line between the online world and real life.


Tommo barks instructions, both to those on the streets and beaches where he is and to those watching the stream on their phones and computers. At one point, he notices three coaches poised to take the arriving migrants away and decides they need to be blocked. He tells one of his comrades to get his car, then turns to the online audience and says: “We need a road blockage at the Eastney entrance of Portsmouth. Someone get down there with a load of cars and put your cars in front of the entrance.” More than once on the stream, he encourages those who are a couple of hours drive away to come and join, reassuring them he will still be there.


His calls only worked to an extent. Tommo’s threat to bring 1,000 men were exaggerated (200 people, seemingly mainly locals, turned out), and his call for a boat blockade to follow the RNLI lifeboats fell flat (the only boat to arrive was a lone kayak). Nonetheless, Tommo was “experimenting with converting an online audience into capacity on the ground,” according to Lewis Nielson, antifascist officer at Stand Up To Racism. For this reason, it would be wrong to dismiss Tommo as a mere grifter, he suggests. “It’s not mere spectacle instead of organisation. The spectacle is itself a technique of organising”, said Nielson.


The arrival of a lifeboat full of asylum seekers to Portsmouth, where Tommo lives, was an opportunity that appeared to fall into his lap. But the day before, a large group of protesters dressed in black and wearing …

author: Γιάννης Βολιάτης
title: Σχετικά με τον εκλογικό θρίαμβο των φασιστών του AfD
content:
Σχετικά με τον εκλογικό θρίαμβο των φασιστών του AfD στην Σαξονία-Άνχαλτ και τις ευθύνες της Αριστεράς και των κινημάτων.


Δεν είναι η “woke κουλτούρα”. Είναι η ταξική πάλη.


Μετά την αναμενόμενη μεγάλη νίκη της ακροδεξιάς του AfD στην Σαξονία-Άνχαλτ – η οποία μάλλον προαναγγέλλει και μια μελλοντική παρόμοια εικόνα σε ολόκληρη την Γερμανία – είδα πολλούς νεοσυντηρητικούς της Αριστεράς να διατρανώνουν πως η κύρια αιτία βρίσκεται μέσα στην ίδια την σύγχρονη Αριστερά, την μορφή και τα προτάγματά της.


Σαν μια αφαιρετική προσέγγιση και χωρίς να πολυκοιτάξει κάνεις τι ακριβώς εννοεί ο ποιητής, θα μπορούσε κάποιος να συμφωνήσει. Πράγματι, η Αριστερά, ιδίως στην Δύση, έχει παίξει τον ρόλο της ως μη αξιόπιστη λύση για την εργατική τάξη, ενώ τα κινήματα γενικότερα έχουν αποτύχει να εκπληρώσουν τον ιστορικό κοινωνικό – πολιτικό τους ρόλο, του αναρχικού – ελευθεριακού συμπεριλαμβανομένου αν θέλουμε να είμαστε ειλικρινείς.


Όταν όμως διαβάσει κάποιος λίγο πιο βαθιά τις αιτιάσεις και το φταίξιμο που αποδίδει αυτή η κριτική στην ευρύτερη Αριστερά, καταλαβαίνει πως κάτι πάει πολύ λάθος με την εποχή μας γενικά και πως η κυριαρχία των αξιών και της ιδεολογίας της αστικής τάξης επάνω στην εργατική αλλά και τα κινήματα της, είναι πολύ πιο διευρυμένη από όσο νομίζουμε, και με πολλούς και διάφορους τρόπους.


Λένε λοιπόν αυτές οι κριτικές πως το φταίξιμο της Αριστεράς (και των κινημάτων ευρύτερα) είναι πως παράτησαν τον εργατικό, λαϊκό, ταξικό λόγο. Όλα καλά ως εδώ, καθότι αυτό ισχύει σε μεγάλο βαθμό για ένα σημαντικό κομμάτι της Δυτικής κυρίως Αριστεράς, ιδίως της Ευρωπαϊκής. Κάπου εδώ όμως σταματάει το καλό και ξεκινάνε τα παρατραγουδά.


Σύμφωνα με τις κριτικές αυτές, η Αριστερά έχει αντικαταστήσει τον ταξικό-λαϊκό με τον “δικαιωματικό”, τον “woke” λόγο. Ασχολήθηκε υπερβολικά με το έμφυλο ζήτημα, τους μετανάστες και όλα αυτά που (δήθεν) δεν αφορούν τις πλατιές εργατικές μάζες που δυσκολεύονται να τα βγάλουν πέρα. Παρόμοιες (θετικές όμως) κριτικές είχαν ασκήσει και κατά την επιτυχία του Μαμντάνι στην Νέα Υόρκη, λέγοντας πως ο νυν Δήμαρχος νίκησε το δεξιό αλλά και το κεντρώο-φιλελεύθερο κατεστημένο επειδή άφησε δήθεν πίσω του την “woke agenta” και ασχολήθηκε με τα καθημερινά υλικά προβλήματα των φτωχότερων τάξεων. Κάτι που, σύμφωνα με τους φωστήρες της συντηρητικής Αριστεράς, δεν έκαναν οι ομόσταβλοί του στην Ευρώπη –και ιδίως στην Γερμανία- και έτσι δόθηκε χώρος στους Ναζί να απευθυνθούν στους εργαζόμενους και να τους κάνουν να στρέψουν την οργή τους στην αντίθετη κατεύθυνση από εκεί που πρέπει.


Φυσικά, αυτή η ανάλυση έχει τόση σχέση με τα προτάγματα της οποιασδήποτε Αριστεράς, όση έχει και ο φασισμός με τα συμφέροντα της εργατικής τάξης.  Ενώ φυσικά ένα μεγάλο κομμάτι της εξευγενισμένης Αριστεράς, αυτής που φυτοζωεί στον Δυτικό Καπιταλισμό, παράτησε όντως εντελώς τον ταξικό λόγο και την εργατική απεύθυνση, το ζήτημα δεν είναι φυσικά ότι ξεκίνησε ή συνέχισε να μιλάει για τις μειονότητες, τους μετανάστες, τα lgbtqi+ άτομα κλπ. Οποιοσδήποτε έχει την παραμικρή σχέση με την ιδέα της κοινωνικής απελευθέρωσης, το ευρύτερο εργατικό κίνημα κλπ, αντιλαμβάνεται πως ταξική πολιτική χωρίς ευθεία και αδιαπραγμάτευτη υπεράσπιση των κοινωνικά βαλλόμενων ομάδων και των δικαιωμάτων τους, απλά δεν υπάρχει. Το “συμφέρον του Έλληνα, Γερμανού, Ιταλού” κλπ εργάτη δεν μπορεί να τεθεί απέναντι σε οποιουδήποτε μετανάστη, ούτε και η ενασχόληση με το έμφυλο ζήτημα μπορεί να μπει σε κάποιο ζύγι σε σχέση με τις εργατικές διεκδικήσεις. Αντίθετα, οι τελευταίες, αν δεν συμπεριλαμβάνουν την ολότητα της εργατικής τάξης -που αποτελείται από cis άνδρες, cis γυναίκες, gay queer, trans, λευκούς, μαύρες κλπ- τότε είναι πιο αδύναμες και ελλιπείς.


Ίσως αυτό να είναι κάτι το οποίο δεν χώνεψε ποτέ πολύ καλά, τόσο η νεοφιλελέφτ Αριστερά από την μία – που οικειοποιήθηκε τον φιλελεύθερο, ατομοκεντρικό λόγο σε σχέση με αυτά τα ζητήματα- όσο και αυτή που της ασκεί την κριτική, δηλαδή η συντηρητική, η “πατριωτική”, η δήθεν “πιο λαϊκή” Αριστερά. Ίσως βέβαια και να το καταλάβαιναν, αλλά, έχοντας αμφότερες εντελώς διαφορετικές προτεραιότητες και ευκαιριακές τακτικές, το αγνόησαν. Και εξ αιτίας αυτής της αδυναμίας κατανόησης ή συνειδητής αγνόησης, δεν κατάφεραν ποτέ να περάσουν αυτό το απλό μήνυμα στους δοκιμαζόμενους από την φτώχεια εργάτες και εργάτριες: Το Κεφάλαιο μας θέλει διαιρεμένους/ες για να είμαστε πιο αδύναμοι/ες. Για αυτό και υπερτονίζει και οξύνει τις διαφορές μεταξύ μας.


Αν όμως θα έπρεπε να αναδείξουμε ένα σφάλμα της φιλελέφτ Δυτικής Αριστεράς, αυτό δεν είναι …

author: Unknown
title: The anti-Kurdish climate
content:
Great expectations, anxieties, hopes and countless unanswered questions surrounded the process when the proposal known as the “Framework Law” was enacted on 10 August 2026 under the title “Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration”. The law did not meet every expectation or dispel every concern. It did, however, once again demonstrate Abdullah Öcalan’s determination to remove weapons from the equation and build peace. With a resolve few would dare to show, he set aside details that could lead the issue into a deadlock and, in a manner befitting a leader, identified the resulting framework as the fundamental basis for a solution. He stressed the importance of responsible and understanding approaches by both sides in giving substance to this framework and putting it into practice. He brought a democratic and solution-oriented spirit to a structure that carries risks and problems, thereby contributing significantly to giving the law meaning. The task now was to imbue this framework with a spirit capable of carrying the issue towards a democratic solution. That would depend on how the law was implemented in practice.


The process has indeed entered an extremely critical stage. It may not yet have suffered a derailment, but the road itself has been subjected to damage that makes such an accident possible. Several significant developments following the enactment of the Framework Law have caused concern among all those approaching the process with a sense of responsibility.


The Kurdish people first mourned their own losses as the Freedom Movement announced martyrs whose deaths it had been unable to make public during the period of intense warfare. This was the most fundamental human right of a people. Tending to these deep wounds, whose scars can never fully disappear, and fulfilling final duties in this healing season of peace were acts of dignity that no law could restrict. Respecting these ceremonies held by the Kurdish people and observing them without interference was a test of whether the state, which bears responsibility for this painful history, could inspire confidence in the process. Instead, even these acts of mourning appeared to be begrudged to the Kurdish people, as the issue was approached through the familiar reflexes of a cold and authoritarian state mentality. The people were effectively subjected to finger-wagging. For the sake of the state’s arrogance, salt was rubbed into the wounds of an entire people.


Another development that raised concern at such a critical time was the circulation of certain notes that Abdullah Öcalan described as a conspiracy and provocation. This was by no means an ordinary matter. It was an act of special warfare against the Kurdish Freedom Movement, designed to have an impact both within and outside the movement. The circulation of certain texts as meeting notes, their manipulation to provide material for perception operations, and attempts to cast a shadow over the dialogue and negotiation process through selectively extracted and decontextualised remarks were clearly planned. Most dangerous of all was the targeting of Abdullah Öcalan, the central figure whose role makes this process unique and who most directly determines its success and future.


Another issue emerged in the rhetoric that spilled over from political platforms into football stands and onto the pitch. It was clear that attempts were being made to turn Amed, a city whose meaning for the Kurdish people extends far beyond its geographical boundaries, and the football club built there through immense effort into a source of controversy. Like anyone else, the Kurdish people took pride in and celebrated the club’s achievements after its promotion to a higher league. Yet they were subjected first to threats from fascist groups emboldened in Turkey, followed by hostility from political circles and threats from the highest levels of the state. Even the most innocent forms of belonging that bring Kurds together, foster unity and create shared values were treated as threats and turned into grounds for social division. Some went even further. This mentality, which begrudged an entire people their success and joy and sought to portray them as defeated, insecure and guilty, was unwilling to regard Kurds as equals even on the football pitch.


These three major developments were highly dangerous not only because of the consequences they produced, but also because of the perception operations aimed …

author: Unknown
title: Communiqué vom revolutionären Block an der Pride Aargau 2026
content:
Am 5. September haben wir uns zusammengetan und einen starken, lauten und sichtbaren revolutionären Block auf die Strassen Aaraus getragen. Wir haben uns den Raum genommen, den wir brauchen, und damit gezeigt: Pride lässt sich nicht auf Konsum und bunte Logos reduzieren. Pride ist politisch und wir haben sie selbstbestimmt politisch gemacht.


Die Geschichte unserer Bewegung beginnt nicht mit Sponsoren, CSD-Bühnen oder Regenbogenwerbung. Sie beginnt mit Widerstand. Stonewall war kein harmloses Fest und kein höflicher Appell an die Mächtigen. Es war ein Aufstand von Menschen, die sich gegen Polizeigewalt, Repression und eine Gesellschaft gewehrt haben, die ihnen keinen Platz zugestehen wollte. Gerade deshalb ist es fatal, wenn heute versucht wird, Pride zu entpolitisieren.


Gleichzeitig erklärt die Leitung der Pride Aargau ihre Demonstration selbst als «explizit politische Aktion für queere Rechte und Anliegen» und fordert queere Fahnen, Plakate und Banner. Wer daraus dennoch ableitet, Politik müsse vor den Toren der Pride Halt machen, widerspricht dem Ursprung und dem Charakter unserer Bewegung.


Wir lassen uns unsere Politik nicht vorgeben.


STONEWALL WAS A RIOT — WE WON'T BE QUIET!


Eine queere Befreiung, die an nationalen Grenzen endet, bleibt unvollständig. Unsere Kämpfe sind miteinander verbunden – mit feministischen Kämpfen, antirassistischem Widerstand und den Kämpfen gegen Kolonialismus, Besatzung und kapitalistische Ausbeutung.


Deshalb haben wir auch dieses Jahr unmissverständlich gesagt:


NO PRIDE IN GENOCIDE!


Während in Gaza Menschen getötet, vertrieben und ihrer Lebensgrundlagen beraubt werden, darf eine Pride nicht so tun, als hätte all das nichts mit unserer politischen Verantwortung zu tun. Für uns ist Solidarität nicht davon abhängig, ob sie bequem ist oder in das Bild einer unpolitischen Feier passt.


Queere Menschen existieren überall. Auch in Palästina kämpfen sie gegen Queerfeindlichkeit und patriarchale Verhältnisse. Ihre Existenz darf nicht dazu benutzt werden, eine ganze Bevölkerung zu entmenschlichen oder Besatzung und staatliche Gewalt zu legitimieren.


Wir weigern uns, Menschen gegeneinander ausspielen zu lassen. Wer Queerfeindlichkeit bekämpft, darf nicht gleichzeitig Rassismus und Islamfeindlichkeit fördern. Wer gegen patriarchale Gewalt einsteht, darf nicht darüber schweigen, wenn Menschen unter Besatzung, Vertreibung und einem Genozid leiden.


Solidarität bedeutet, die Widersprüche auszuhalten und trotzdem gemeinsam gegen Unterdrückung zu kämpfen.


Von Aarau bis Palästina, von der feministischen Bewegung in Rojava bis zu den queeren Kämpfen weltweit: Unsere Kämpfe sind miteinander verbunden.


HOCH DIE INTERNATIONALE SOLIDARITÄT!


Pride hat eine Geschichte des Widerstands gegen die Polizei. Und diese Geschichte ist nicht einfach abgeschlossen.


Auch an unserer Pride waren Repression und Kontrolle präsent. Mehrfach versuchten die Bullen, unseren Demozug zu stoppen. Durch die grosse Masse unseres Blocks, unsere Entschlossenheit und unseren Zusammenhalt konnten sie das nicht durchsetzen.


Das ist für uns kein nebensächlicher Zwischenfall. Eine Institution, die für Ordnung sorgt, setzt immer auch fest, wessen Sicherheit, wessen Freiheit und wessen Interessen geschützt werden. Queere Menschen erleben polizeiliche Kontrolle und Repression nicht unabhängig von Rassismus, Klassenzugehörigkeit, Geschlecht oder Aufenthaltsstatus.


Wir haben deshalb keinen Grund, der Polizei für ihre vermeintliche «Schutzfunktion» dankbar zu sein.


Unsere Befreiung wird nicht von oben verteilt. Sie wird erkämpft – auf der Strasse, in unseren Communities und durch Organisierung.


BOTTOM AND TOPS — WE ALL HATE COPS!


Ein Regenbogen auf einem Firmenlogo verändert keine gesellschaftlichen Verhältnisse.


Während Unternehmen & Parteien Pride als Marketingfläche nutzen, bleiben Ausbeutung, soziale Ungleichheit und Abhängigkeiten bestehen. Unsere Identitäten werden verkauft, unsere Kämpfe zur Marke gemacht und unsere Wut in Konsum verwandelt. Genau darin liegt das Problem des Rainbow Capitalism: Nicht unsere Befreiung steht im Zentrum, sondern die Frage, wie sich mit unserer Existenz Profit machen lässt.


Eine Pride, die sich problemlos vermarkten lässt, stellt für die bestehenden Verhältnisse keine Bedrohung dar.


Eine Pride, die über Sichtbarkeit hinausgeht, schon.


Wir wollen nicht nur akzeptiert werden, solange wir gute Konsumentinnen, Angestellte oder Kundinnen sind. Wir wollen keine …

author: Unknown
title: AfD’nin yükselişi Almanya'da Türkiyelileri ve diğer azınlıkları kaygılandırdı
content:
Saksonya-Anhalt Anayasayı Koruma Teşkilatı tarafından aşırı sağcı olarak sınıflandırılan Almanya İçin Alternatif’in (AfD) eyalet seçimlerinde yüzde 43,8 oyla birinci parti çıkması, Almanya’daki Türkiyeliler ve aşırı sağın hedef aldığı diğer toplumsal kesimlerde kaygıyla karşılandı.


Almanya Türk Toplumu (TGD), özellikle göçmenler, Müslümanlar, Yahudiler, LGBTİ+’lar ve aşırı sağın hedef aldığı diğer gruplar için daha güçlü ve kalıcı güvenlik önlemleri alınmasını istedi.


TGD Eş Başkanı


Mehtap Çağlar, seçim sonucunun yalnızca siyasi oranlardan ibaret olmadığını belirterek birçok insanın kendi güvenliğini sorguladığını söyledi: “İnsanlar çocuklarının okula korkmadan gidip gidemeyeceğini, sokakta güvende olup olmadıklarını ve bu ülkede kendilerini hâlâ ait hissedip hissedemeyeceklerini düşünüyor.”


Diğer Eş Başkan Gökay Sofuoğlu da federal hükümet ile Saksonya-Anhalt yönetimine, ırkçı, antisemitik, Müslüman ve LGBTİ+ karşıtı saldırıların mağdurlarına yönelik danışmanlık, koruma ve önleme hizmetlerini güçlendirme çağrısı yaptı. Sofuoğlu, siyasi tehditlerin şiddete dönüşmesinin beklenmemesi, mağdurların başvurabileceği güvenilir kurumlara yeterli kaynak ayrılması gerektiğini söyledi.


“Bizi istemeyenler aslında bize ihtiyaç duyacak”


TGD, aşırı sağın dışlayıcı politikalarının Saksonya-Anhalt’ın ekonomik ve demografik geleceğini de tehdit edeceğine dikkat çekti. Eyalette önümüzdeki on yılda yaklaşık 200 bin kişilik işgücü açığı oluşmasının beklendiğini belirtti.


Çağlar, insanların kökenleri, inançları veya cinsel kimlikleri nedeniyle kendilerini güvende hissetmemelerinin eyaletin kendisine zarar vereceğini söyledi:


“İnsanları ülkeden veya toplumdan uzaklaştırmak Saksonya-Anhalt’ın kendisine zarar verir. Ailelerimiz, işimiz, dostluklarımız ve evimiz burada. Bizi istemeyenler aslında bize ihtiyaç duyacak. Her şeyden önce devletin anayasal görevi bizi korumaktır.”


TGD ayrıca Saksonya-Anhalt’taki demokratik partilere AfD ile işbirliği ve siyasi tavizlere karşı oluşturulan “yangın duvarını” koruma çağrısı yaptı.


Mülteci örgütü: İnsan hakları pazarlık konusu olamaz


Kaygıya  kapılanlar, yalnızca Türkiyeliler değil. Seçimden 11 gün önce Magdeburg’da işletme sahibi yaklaşık 160 göçmen, ırkçılık ve ayrımcılığa karşı bir günlük dükkân kapatma eylemi yapmıştı.


Saksonya-Anhalt Mülteciler Konseyi’nden Saaeid Saaeid, seçimden sonra uzun yıllardır eyalette yaşayan göçmenlerin bile burada kalıp kalmamayı sorguladıklarını söyledi. Saaeid, “Henüz nasıl bir hükümet kurulacağını bilmiyoruz ama bu sonuçların şimdiden nasıl bir korku yarattığını biliyoruz” dedi.


Konsey, tehdit altındaki insanları desteklemeye devam edeceğini açıklarken, Saaeid, “İnsan hakları siyasetin pazarlık konusu haline getirilemez” diye konuştu.


Yahudi toplumu: “Burası bizim ülkemiz”


Saksonya-Anhalt Yahudi Cemaatleri Eyalet Birliği de demokratik temel değerlerin ve azınlıkların kararlılıkla korunmasını, güvenlik önlemlerinin güçlendirilmesini ve toplumsal çeşitliliğin açıkça savunulmasını istedi.


Yahudilerin Saksonya-Anhalt’ta bin yılı aşkın bir geçmişi bulunduğunu hatırlatan Birlik, “Burası bizim ülkemiz; Yahudi ailelerin kuşaklar boyunca yaşadığı, çocuklarımızın ülkesi” dedi.


Almanya Yahudileri Merkez Konseyi Başkanı


Josef Schuster seçim sonucundan “kişisel olarak dehşete düştüğünü” söyledi. Halle’de yaşayan Yahudi aktivist Igor Matviyets ise ortaya çıkan durumu “ürkütücü bir belirsizlik hali” olarak tanımladı; toplumsal hafıza, din özgürlüğü ve başkalarının acısıyla dayanışma konusundaki uzlaşmanın aşınmasından kaygı duyduğunu belirtti.


Engelliler için “ilan edilmiş dışlama”


Federal Ayrımcılıkla Mücadele Sorumlusu Ferda Ataman, göçmenler ve çocuklarının yanı sıra Yahudilerin, Müslümanların, LGBTİ+’ların ve engellilerin de seçim sonucundan özellikle kaygı duyduklarını söyledi. Ataman, azınlıklara ve farklı düşünenlere yönelik kampanyaların ayrımcılığa veya doğrudan şiddete dönüşmesinden korkulduğunu belirtti.


Sosyal Birlik VdK Başkanı Verena Bentele ile örgütün Saksonya-Anhalt Başkanı Lutz Schütte-Krietsch ise AfD’nin okullarda kapsayıcı eğitime son verme vaadine dikkat çekerek bunu engelliler açısından “ilan edilmiş dışlama” olarak nitelendirdi.


Göçmen örgütleri: AfD’ye iktidar yolu açılmamalı


Almanya’daki göçmen örgütlerinin çatı yapılarından Göçmen Örgütleri Federal Konferansı

 

(BKMO) diğer partilerden AfD ile koalisyon kurmamalarını, AfD’nin dışarıdan desteğine dayanmamalarını ve AfD oylarıyla çoğunluk oluşturmamalarını …

author: Jake Johnson
title: German Far Right Party AfD Wins Regional Election, Thanks Musk for Support
content:
Alternative for Germany won the most votes in the Saxony-Anhalt election but fell short of an absolute majority.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

The far-right Alternative for Germany party thanked the world’s richest man, Elon Musk, after decisively winning a key regional election on Sunday, sparking alarm across Europe and around the globe.

Ulrich Siegmund, AfD’s lead candidate in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, praised Musk — who has openly advocated for the far-right, xenophobic party — for his support and “clear and highly important perspective on the political developments of our time — including here in Germany.” Siegmund wrote that if AfD ends up leading the state government, the party “would very much welcome the opportunity for strong and constructive cooperation,” adding that “Germany would once again be a place worth investing in.”

Siegmund’s post on the social media platform X, which Musk owns, came after AfD won just over 44% of the vote in the Saxony-Anhalt election, trouncing the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz. CDU finished a distant second with 17.1% of the vote.

“Well done!” Musk wrote, in German, following AfD’s election win. The mega-billionaire has called AfD “the only hope for Germany.”

US President Donald Trump, a political ally of Musk, posted to Truth Social a screenshot of exit polls showing AfD leading the regional election on Sunday afternoon.

“Leave it to Trump to celebrate the victory of a far-right German party that shows sympathy for the Nazis, downplays the Holocaust, and flirts with Putin,” Kenneth Roth, the former executive director of Human Rights Watch, wrote on social media in response to the US president.

The Associated Press noted that “to win an absolute majority, AfD needed to clinch 42 of the 83 seats in the state parliament, but the party appeared on track to win 39. Depending on the ultimate make-up of parliament, it could still end up leading the state government.” Siegmund would be the first far-right leader to govern a German state since 1945.

But other German parties have refused to work with AfD, raising doubts about its ability to form a government in Saxony-Anhalt, which has a population of around 2.1 million people.

David Adler, co-general coordinator of the Progressive International, wrote that the election “sent a clear message, to Germany as to all of Europe, that the far-right rampage is not slowing down, but accelerating instead.”

AfD focuses heavily on immigration, vowing “deportation from minute one” and calling for abolition of “the fundamental right to asylum.”

“In addition to deporting immigrants, the party has proposed cutting funding for public broadcasters, banning gay pride flags in schools, and teaching more Russian, as well as tax breaks for large families and free childcare,” The New York Times reported. The newspaper noted that Siegmund declined to condemn supporters who “chanted his surname… in the style of the Nazi salute, ‘Sieg Heil.’”

European officials voiced deep concern about AfD’s surge in the regional election, with France’s Europe minister calling the results “a serious moment.”

“Nationalism and xenophobia will never be a solution,” said Benjamin Haddad. “We must listen with humility to the anger, the concerns, the fears, and respond to them. We cannot forget our history. That is the meaning behind the choices made by France and Germany.”

Spanish Julen Bollain wrote on social media that “the far-right is managing to turn discontent, economic insecurity, and disaffection into votes.”

“AfD is doing something that should especially worry the left: transforming precarity, frustration, and disaffection into political identity and votes,” Bollain added. “And if we don’t manage to give a collective response to the existing social discontent, someone always shows up ready to turn it into fear, hate, and scapegoats. And there they beat us, because they move like fish in water.”

As Trump cracks down on political speech, independent media is increasingly necessary.

title: Cezasızlık her yerde
content:
Son dönemde Orta Doğu Teknik Üniversitesinde (ODTÜ) gündeme gelen cinsel şiddet ve saldırı vakaları, Türkiye’de uygulanan cezasızlık politikalarının yaşamın birçok alanında görünür hale geldiğini gösteriyor. Haklarında şiddet iddiaları olan ODTÜ Elektrik ve Elektronik Mühendisliği bölümü öğrencisi Y. E. Ö. ve aynı üniversitenin Biyolojik Bilimler Bölümü araştırma görevlisi İ.K.Ö. hakkında mağdurların başlattıkları yargı süreci devam ediyor. Konuştuğumuz ODTÜ öğrencileri, yargının işlevsizliğinin üniversite ortamında güvensizliğe sebep olduğunu ifade ediyor. İ.K.Ö. için ODTÜ'de açılan soruşturmanın aylardır sonuçlanmaması ise, öğrenciler tarafından tepkiyle karşılanıyor.

ODTÜ’de kadın ve LGBTİ alanında çalışmalar yürüten Toplumsal Cinsiyet Çalışmaları Topluluğu yaşanan olaylara dair iktidarın politikalarını işaret etti:

“İktidarın artan cezasızlık politikalarını artık kampüsümüzde de net bir şekilde hissedebiliyoruz. Bugün bu iki ayrı vaka birbirinden bağımsız, münferit olaylar olarak değerlendirilmemeli. Her iki mağdur kadının da ortaya koydukları irade bizim bu vakaları görmemizi sağladı fakat okulumuzda hâlâ bilmediğimiz taciz ve şiddet olayları bulunuyor. Biz bu vakaların iktidarın izlediği politikalar ve atanmış rektörün de kampüsümüzdeki yönetiminin bir sonucu olduğunu vurgulamak istiyoruz. Biyolojik Bilimler Bölümü’nde yaşanan süreç bize açıkça gösteriyor ki hakkında darp, ısrarlı takip ve cinsel istismar iddiaları bulunan bir bölüm asistanının öğrencilerle ve kampüsle bağı korunuyor. İktidarın cezasızlık politikaları, rektörlüğün tutumu ve failin babasının savcı oluşuyla beraber görüyoruz ki mağdur değil, fail korunuyor. Faillere kampüste hâlâ alan tanınıyor. Herhangi bir yaptırım uygulanmıyor. Bu cezasızlık başka olaylar için faillere cesaret veriyor ya da mağdurun konuşmasını engelliyor.”

Toplumsal Cinsiyet Çalışmaları Topluluğu mücadelenin devam edeceğini söylerken taleplerini de sıraladı: “ODTÜ’de öğrenciler buna karşın sessiz kalmıyor yürüyüşlerle, basın açıklamalarıyla ve imza kampanyalarıyla bu hukuksuzluğun karşısında bir mücadele örüyor. Bunlara karşın güvenli kampüs, faillerin cezalandırılması ve cinsel tacizi önlemek adına verilen eğitimlerin zorunlu hale getirilmesi taleplerimizi kampüsün her yerinde yükseltmeye devam edeceğiz. Güvenli kampüsü ellerimizle kuracağız.”

Y. E. Ö. davasına ilişkin konuştuğumuz bir ODTÜ öğrencisi: “Refika Aksoy Yurdu'nda konaklayan bir kadın ve ODTÜ'lü bir öğrenci olarak, failin adli tıp raporuna ve çeşitli delillere rağmen yurdumuzda kalmaya devam etmesinden büyük bir rahatsızlık duyuyorum. Kendi güvenliğimize dair endişelerimiz hiçe sayılıyor ve önlem taleplerimiz reddediliyor. Yürüyüş ve basın açıklamalarında oluşturduğumuz kamuoyu ısrarla görmezden geliniyor. Karma bir yurtta nitelikli cinsel saldırı suçundan yargılanan birinin kalmasına izin verilerek öğrencileri korumaya karşı çıkılıyor; yargıda sıkça karşımıza çıkan hukuksuzluk ve öğrencilerin haklı endişeleri yok sayılarak fail korunuyor. Kendi yaşam alanımızda bile güvende hissetmiyoruz. Bizim için değil, bize karşı çalışan bir yönetim var.”

Okul yönetiminin ve mahkemenin tutumunu eleştiren öğrenci “Oluşturmaya çalıştıkları korku iklimine teslim olmayacağız, fail hak ettiği cezayı alana ve yurt ve kampüsten uzaklaştırılana kadar sesimizi duyurmaya devam edeceğiz” sözlerini ekleyerek mücadeleye devam edeceklerini söyledi.

Bu iki sürece ilişkin Refika Aksoy yurdunda kalan başka bir öğrenci ise, okulda güvensiz hissetmeye başladıklarına vurgu yaptı: “ODTÜ’de okumaya başladığımda kampüsün görece güvenli olması, gece ya da gündüz kampüste rahatça hareket edebilmek benim için çok değerliydi. Kampüs, dışarıdaki güvensizlik hissinden bir nebze olsun uzaklaşabildiğim, kendimi daha özgür hissettiğim bir yerdi. Ancak nitelikli cinsel saldırı sanığı Y. E.Ö.’nün ODTÜ yurtlar bölgesinde barınabildiğini öğrenmek, bu güven duygusunu ciddi biçimde sarstı. Bunun hemen ardından Biyolojik Bilimler Bölümü’nde görev yapan İ.K.Ö. hakkındaki taciz iddialarını öğrenmek ise öfkemi daha da büyüttü. Çünkü üniversiteler yalnızca ders aldığımız, sınavlara girdiğimiz yerler değil; günümüzün çok büyük bir bölümünü geçirdiğimiz, yaşadığımız alanlar. Bu nedenle kampüste kadınların kendilerini güvende hissedebilmesi bir ayrıcalık değil, en temel haklarımızdan biri.”

title: Behördenversagen ist kein Einzelfall
content:
NSU, Neukölln, Hanau. „Futur Drei“-Regisseur Faraz Shariats neuer Justizthriller „Staatsschutz“ zeigt den Kampf gegen rechten Terror und institutionellen Rassismus in der Justiz.

Seyo Kim ist frisch ausgebildete Staatsanwältin in einer ostdeutschen Stadt. Ihre Wohnung hat sie gerade erst bezogen, die Kartons sind noch unausgepackt. In einer der ersten Szenen muss sie in einem Fall für Freispruch plädieren, aus Mangel an Beweisen. Auf der anderen Seite des Gerichtssaals sitzt ein Mann, der aussieht, als könnte er ein Nazi sein. Die Justiz hat ihre Regeln, das muss auch Seyos Idealismus aushalten. Schon bald befindet Seyo sich aber auf der anderen Seite des Justizsystems. Als sie durch einen Park radelt, wird sie von einem anderen Fahrer unter einer Brücke von ihrem Rad gestoßen. Ein Komplize des Angreifers bewirft sie von der Brücke mit einem Molotowcocktail. Schnell befreit sie sich von ihrer brennenden Jacke. Trotz des Schocks und ihrer Verletzungen funktioniert sie sofort, weiß, was jetzt wichtig ist. Der rassistische Anschlag verändert Seyo. Sie schneidet sich die Haare, scheint rougher und unangepasster aufzutreten als zuvor. Ihre Freundin schenkt ihr eine Kette – eine Art Talisman, den sie fortan immer trägt. Seyo schafft es, einen der Täter vor Gericht zu bringen. Entschlossen, sich zu verteidigen und ihre Angreifer zur Rechenschaft zu ziehen, nutzt sie ihren Zugang zu Informationen in der Staatsanwaltschaft. Ein Kollege wirft ihr vor, sie würde versuchen, sich durch ihre Rolle einen Vorteil zu verschaffen. Doch vielmehr versucht Seyo, die Nachteile, denen sie ausgesetzt ist, auszugleichen. Denn wie bald immer deutlicher wird, gibt es Verstrickungen ihrer Behörde mit den Angeklagten und Unklarheiten in alten Fällen, von denen sie einen Zusammenhang mit ihrem vermutet. author: Unknown
title: Kadını öldürmeye teşebbüs etti, iddianame bile yazılmadı!
content:
Türkiye’de erkek şiddeti, kadına yönelik şiddet neden azalmıyor? Bu soruya verilecek en net yanıtlardan biri hiç kuşkusuz yargının cezasızlık politikası.


Peki nedir bu cezasızlık politikası? Feminist hareketin “Erkek adalet değil, gerçek adalet” diye sloganlaştırdığı meselenin özü tam olarak nereye dayanıyor? 


İsterseniz bunu kâğıt üzerindeki süslü maddelerden değil, somut bir şiddet vakası üzerinden adım adım irdeleyelim.


Yoğun bakıma alındı


S.T. isimli erkek, Aralık 2025’te Bodrum’da yaşayan komşusu G.E.’ye öldürmeye teşebbüs eti, bıçakla saldırdı. 


Saldırı sonucunda G.E.'nin vücudunda çoklu kesikler, iç kanama, kas ve sinir yaralanmaları ile acil müdahale gerektiren ağır tendon ve sinir kesikleri oluştu. Öyle ki Adli Tıp Kurumu raporuyla da sabit olduğu üzere bu saldırı "kasten yaralama" değil, hayati tehlike içeren ağır bir şiddet eylemiydi.


14–15 Aralık 2025'te G.E. yoğun bakıma alındı. Hayati tehlikesinin devam ettiği bu süreçte tıbbi stabilizasyonu sağlandı.


16 Aralık’ta yaralanmaların ciddiyeti ve boyutu nedeniyle G.E., İzmir’e sevk edildi. Burada tendon, sinir ve kas onarımları için ağır mikrocerrahi operasyon geçirdi.


İlgili tıbbi raporlar, tutanaklar ve diğer tüm resmi belgeler eksiksiz düzenlendi. Bu belgelerin tamamı, saldırının ağırlığını ve hayati tehlikeyi net bir şekilde ortaya koyuyordu.


Nihayetinde Bodrum Cumhuriyet Savcılığı tarafından soruşturma başlatıldı ve şüpheli S.T. tutuklandı.


Peki tutuklandı da ne oldu? Bu sırada yargı mercileri ne yapmalıydı, neyi yapmadı?


Aksayan soruşturma ve cezasızlık süreci


Aralık 2025 ile Nisan 2026 arasındaki soruşturma sürecinde tam anlamıyla bir ihmaller zinciri. Mesela, görgü tanıkları olmasına rağmen tanık ifadeleri alınmadı. Mesela, karşı tarafın birbiriyle çelişkili ifadeleri olmasına rağmen soruşturma derinleştirilmedi.


Olay anına dair video kayıtları araştırılmadı, incelenmedi. Soruşturma dosyasında bir türlü iddianame hazırlanmadı. Haliyle bir duruşma tarihi bile belirlenmedi.


Ve sonuç olarak 7 Nisan 2026’da, yani saldırıdan yaklaşık 4 ay sonra şüpheli S.T. tahliye edildi.


Tahliye sonrası ne oldu dersiniz? 


Saldırının tekrarlanma ihtimali nedeniyle G.E. için gerçek, somut ve çok yakın bir hayati risk oluştu. Belirsizlik ve korumasızlık durumu kadının yaşamını çekilmez hale getirdi.


Devam eden bu hayati risk nedeniyle G.E., 6284 sayılı Kanun kapsamında Aile Mahkemesine başvurdu. Mahkemeden, şüpheli hakkında uzaklaştırma kararı verilmesi, elektronik kelepçe takılması, mesafeli koruma tedbirinin uygulanması, varsa silahlarının toplatılması ve kararlara uymaması halinde zorlama hapsi uygulanacağına dair ihtar yapılması talep edildi.


Şüphelinin tahliye edilmiş olması ve iddianamenin hâlâ hazırlanmaması nedeniyle, bugün hâlâ uzaklaştırma kararının uzatılması, elektronik kelepçe tedbirinin devamı ile mesafe ve adres bazlı koruma tedbirlerinin sürdürülmesi için düzenli olarak uzatma taleplerinde bulunuluyor.


Kadını öldüresiye döven, bıçakla ağır şekilde yaralayan erkek şu anda ev hapsinde. Kadın ise koruma kararı bittikçe adliye koridorlarında yeni başvurular yapmak zorunda bırakılıyor.


Aradan neredeyse bir yıl geçmesine rağmen iddianame hâlâ hazırlanmadı. Hazırlanmadığı gibi soruşturma hâlen "basit yaralama" üzerinden yürütülüyor.


Oysa G.E.’nin avukatı

Sena Yazıbağlı Selanik

, soruşturmanın yaralama suçundan değil, "kasten öldürmeye teşebbüs" suçundan ilerletilmesi ve iddianamenin bu suçlamayla yazılması gerektiğini vurguluyor.


Avukat Selanik, dosyadaki tabloyu şu sözlerle özetliyor: “Hâlen tanıklar dinlenmedi. Aradan geçen bu zaman, ciddi anlamda sağlıksız, mağdur için adil olmayan bir soruşturmaya ve delil karartmaya yol açabilir.”


Bir yıldır dinlenmeyen o tanıkların zaman geçtikçe olayı unutması, ayrıntıları kaçırması mümkün değil mi?


Bir kadın, kendisini öldürmeye teşebbüs etmiş bir erkekten korunmak için daha ne yapacak? Yargının harekete geçmesi için bir kadının daha hayatını kaybetmesi mi gerekiyor?


(EMK)

author: Mag
title: Rassismus, Sexismus und ein Klima der Angst bei der Basler Polizei – nun wissenschaftlich belegt
content:
Dossier


„

Was die unabhängige Personalbefragung der Kantonspolizei Basel-Stadt über die Zustände im Korps aussagt, ist katastrophal: eine Kultur der Angst, eine veraltete Macho-Kultur, ein totaler Vertrauensverlust. (…) Markus Schefer, der Professor für Staats- und Verwaltungsrecht an der Uni Basel ist die erste gewählte Telefonnummer von Journalist*innen, wenn es eine Debatte über das Vorgehen der Polizei bei Demos gibt – er war beauftragt worden, die schiefe Personallage der Polizei zu untersuchen. Unterstützt wurde er von Claudia Puglisi, einer Polizeidirektor*in aus Niedersachsen, die bei der Präsentation neben ihm sass – ihr besorgt wirkender Blick spiegelte die Drastik der Ergebnisse wider. Denn an heftig negativen Begrifflichkeiten mangelt es im 42-seitigen Dokument sicherlich nicht.  (…) Die Kritik konzentriert sich auf Polizeikommandant Martin Roth. Er ist medial angeschlagen, seit linke Politiker*innen im Frühjahr 2023 wegen des

Gummischrot-Einsatzes der Frauentags-Demo


 seinen

Rücktritt


 forderten

…“

Artikel von David Rutschmann vom 21. Juni 2024 in bajour


 („Kein Lodern, ein Flammen“) – u.a. wurden Polizistinnen wurden in «fi**bar» oder «unf**kbar» unterteilt… Siehe dazu mehr Infos:


Das Gummischrot war illegal: Das Basler Appellationsgericht rügt die Polizei wegen eines Einsatzes gegen den feministischen Kampftag 2023


„Jahrelang war es so selten wie eine Fasnacht im Sommer, dass Basler Gerichte der Basler Polizei Grenzen setzen. Das ändert sich glücklicherweise gerade (…). Schritt für Schritt weist die Justiz ein entfesseltes Korps in die Schranken. Das neuste Urteil des Appellationsgerichts, das der WOZ exklusiv vorliegt, ist diesbezüglich ein Meilenstein. Darin erklärt das Gericht das Abfeuern von Gummischrot in eine Menschengruppe, von der keine konkrete Gefahr ausgeht, als illegal. Einen Klassiker der Basler Demobekämpfung. (…) Beurteilt hat das Gericht den Polizeieinsatz gegen den feministischen Kampftag am 8. März 2023. Damals versammelten sich rund 250 Personen vor der Universität. Und wurden, als sie sich in Bewegung setzen wollten, eingekesselt. Kurz darauf begannen die Polizist:innen, mit Gummischrot auf die Demonstrant:innen zu feuern. Doch nur die ersten drei Salven, so das Appellationsgericht, waren verhältnismässig. Diese erfolgten, als sich der Demozug in Richtung der Polizeikette bewegte. Die weiteren Salven waren rechtswidrig. (…) [S]elbst wenn der Mindestabstand eingehalten worden wäre, so das Gericht, hätte das den Gummischroteinsatz nicht gerechtfertigt. Dieser sei rechtswidrig gewesen (…)  In den weiteren Punkten des Urteils zeigt sich dann allerdings, dass auch das Basler Appellationsgericht alten Gewohnheiten nachhängt und noch immer gerne die Argumentation der Polizei übernimmt: Bei der Personenkontrolle sollen Polizistinnen mehreren Demonstrant:innen in die Unterhosen gegriffen haben. Die Polizei bestreitet dies – und das Gericht stellt sich auf ihre Seite. Die objektive Beweislast liege bei den Kläger:innen. In der dritten wichtigen Frage des Urteils geht es um die Rechtmässigkeit des Polizeikessels. Mit einer abenteuerlichen Begründung wischt das Appellationsgericht ein Urteil des Europäischen Gerichtshofs für Menschenrechte (EGMR) vom Tisch, das Anfang 2024 verlangte, dass ein solcher Kessel nicht ohne genau festgelegte Rahmenbedingungen möglich sei, etwa was die Dauer betreffe. In Basel ist das bloss rudimentär geregelt. Mehr sei auch nicht nötig, befindet das Gericht geradezu anmassend: «Diese für eine polizeiliche Technik wie die Einkesselung aussergewöhnlich hohen Anforderungen können für die Schweiz nicht verbindlich sein.» Es reiche aus, dass im Polizeigesetz allgemeines polizeiliches Handeln und Personenkontrollen geregelt seien – auch wenn der Kessel nicht explizit vorkommt. Constanze Seelmann, die die Demonstrant:innen rechtlich vertritt, wird in deren Auftrag den Entscheid ans Bundesgericht weiterziehen. «Das Appellationsgericht hat sich nicht richtig mit dem EGMR-Urteil befasst. Die Schweiz braucht aber ein Grundsatzurteil, ob und falls ja, unter welchen Umständen ein Polizeikessel zulässig ist.» (…) Wie leichtfertig in Basel eingekesselt wird, zeigte sich an der Palästina-Solidemo vergangenen Samstag. (…) Die Demonstrant:innen mussten bis zu zehn Stunden im Kessel ausharren. author: Equality Now
title: Commemorating and celebrating Gloria Steinem: The life and legacy of a feminist trailblazer
content:
3rd September 2026


Commemorating and celebrating Gloria Steinem: The life and legacy of a feminist trailblazer


9 min read


The world has lost an extraordinary champion for equality, and Equality Now has lost a beloved friend, mentor and member of our global family.


Gloria Steinem, the pioneering writer, feminist organiser and political activist, passed away at her New York City home on September 2, 2026, at age 92. For more than half a century, she helped shine a light on women’s rights and gave a voice to generations of women’s beliefs around what was possible for themselves and for each other. 


For Equality Now, Gloria’s loss is deeply personal. Our organisation was founded in her home and she stood alongside us from our earliest days, sharing her voice, wisdom, time and encouragement with extraordinary generosity. She was curious about women around the world, shaped especially by her formative years in India post-college.


“Gloria believed in the beauty of shared power. She used her own powerful voice to make space for millions of women’s voices and generations have stepped into their agency because she did. Her legacy is not only the world she shaped but is embedded in all of us who believe in that vision and continue to strive to achieve it,” said

Mona Sinha

, Chief Executive Officer of Equality Now.


“The world has lost one of its best, and I have lost someone who has been a north star in my own life. I first met Gloria when I was a student at Smith College but was blessed to come to know the woman behind her words and activism. What stays with me is her unconditional love of her chosen family, her extraordinary generosity of spirit, her infectious laugh and her curiosity and zest for women’s lives. For someone whose voice carried so much influence, Gloria had the remarkable ability to make space for everyone. 


“She listened to everyone who came to her Talking Circles. She genuinely wanted to hear your thoughts, your experiences and what you were excited to learn. She had this amazing ability to make everyone feel that their stories, their voices and their ideas mattered, which they did. While I will miss her enormously, I know she walks beside us in every movement she has inspired, in women who have stood up for change and the friendships she has nurtured. Each one of us feels a little braver because she embodied what courage looks like.”


Gloria Steinem’s enduring support for Equality Now and women’s rights


Gloria’s involvement with Equality Now as an active supporter of its mission spans the organisation’s entire 34-year history. She played an integral role as a founding member of Equality Now’s Advisory Board in 1992, served on the Board of Directors from 2010 to 2016, in addition to being a Trustee of Equality Now’s UK entity between 2005 and 2019.


At the United Nations, Gloria publicly supported Equality Now’s ongoing 

Words and Deeds

 campaign, which for almost three decades has highlighted sex discriminatory laws around the world and called for legal reform.


She stood with us against Big Apple Oriental Tours, a New York company promoting sex tourism in Asia, helping press authorities to act in a campaign that ultimately led to legal action against the company and strengthened the case for tougher anti-trafficking laws. 


For over 50 years, Gloria fought to strengthen legal protections for women and girls in the US by championing the Equal Rights Amendment (ERA), which would amend the US Constitution to guarantee equal rights under the law, irrespective of sex. In recent years, she worked alongside Equality Now and the ERA Coalition, helping build pressure on the Biden administration to recognise the ERA.

President Biden declared the ERA the law of the land

 in January 2025.


She was also a longstanding co-chair of Equality Now’s annual Make Equality Reality Gala,  helping the organisation to raise much-needed resources to protect and promote the rights of women and girls globally. In recognition of her tireless work to make equality a reality for everyone, Equality Now honoured Gloria for her lifelong commitment at the 2014

Make Equality Reality Gala

. 


A remarkable life


Born on March 25, 1934, Gloria’s life was a testament to her unwavering commitment to advancing gender equality and in the power of people coming together to create change.


In the 1960s, she made her mark as a journalist covering women’s rights and other social issues. She went on to become one of …

title: Inukjuak man accused of murder was ordered to not contact victim
content:
The Inukjuak man charged with first-degree murder for the death of his partner Elisabeth Qumak had been under a court order to not contact her when she was found dead inside a home in the community. 


Police

found

 the 41-year-old woman with stab wounds on Aug. 24, after Charlie Palliser arrived at the community’s police station to report he had committed a crime. She was pronounced dead at a local health centre.


The 45-year-old already faced charges for a break and enter and assault at Qumak’s home on July 17, court documents reveal. He was released on July 22 with conditions, including that he refrain from contacting her.


The Nunavik Police Service declined to comment on what happened on July 17, saying the investigation has since been handed over to provincial police in Quebec.


When reached by Nunatsiaq News, Quebec police also declined to comment.


Palliser had 

also given a curfew and was expected to attend social services meetings as well as activities organized by non-profit Saqijuq at least twice a month.


According to its website, the organization provides “alternatives to incarceration” by “promoting healthy lifestyles, strengthening cultural connections, and rehabilitating individuals.” It offers activities such as hunting, fishing and camping and workshops revolving around Inuit values and traditions. 


Nunatsiaq News asked Saqijuq if Palliser took part in any of their programs but has yet to hear back.


A Montreal-based coalition

of feminists against domestic violence

 has so far recorded 17 suspected

femicides in the province since the beginning of this year.


The figure is higher than what’s commonly reported in the media because the group monitors gender-based violence in situations that exclude romantic relationships, general co-ordinator Julie Antoine said in an interview. 


“It often happens that men are under no contact orders after a separation that they ultimately end up committing a femicide. Either the crime happens when the woman announces she wants to leave him, or the crime happens happens after an order is issued,” she said.


In about half of these 17 cases, she said, the group

 confirmed that the accused had previously been charged with a violent crime. 


“The state is falling in its role of protecting women, and it’s evident when you see that a high percentage of individuals involved in femicide cases were already known to the justice system,” Antoine said.


Palliser’s next court appearance is scheduled for Dec. 14.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Rosario: movilización contra los femicidios y en reclamo de la emergencia en violencia de género
content:
Las organizaciones decidieron movilizarse luego de que se conocieran tres femicidios en 15 días.


Foto: Aire Libre- Rosario


Escuchar el reporte de Darío Uliassi desde Aire Libre Radio Comunitaria.


Concentraron este miércoles a las 17 frente a la Municipalidad de Rosario y finalizaron con un acto en la puerta de la sede de Gobernación de la provincia en la ciudad.


De la movilización participaron organizaciones feministas, sociales y políticas que se expresaron en contra de la violencia machista y reclamaron justicia por los femicidios.


En la provincia de Santa Fe se registraron más de 30 femicidios en lo que va del año. Además, se contabilizaron 10 víctimas más que en el mismo período del año pasado.


“Paren de matarnos” fue la consigna que encabezó la movilización donde las organizaciones advirtieron por la suba de casos, que se profundizan con el desmantelamiento de las políticas de género en los distintos niveles del Estado.


En declaraciones a Aire Libre, Gabriela Sosa, referente del movimiento feminista Mujeres por la Matria Latinoamericana (Mumalá), exigió la sanción de una ley provincial que declare la emergencia en violencia de género y que se cumpla la ordenanza local que declaró la emergencia hace un tiempo.


“Hemos presentado proyectos para que se declare la emergencia en violencia de género en Santa Fe y también que se pueda aplicar aquella ordenanza de hace varios años que ya declaraba la emergencia en Rosario y que disponía de recursos que siguen estando pendientes”.


Foto: Aire Libre- Rosario


Sosa también denunció las consecuencias del desmantelamiento de políticas públicas: “Esta quita de recursos, a la par de los discursos de odios, comienzan a impactar que las mujeres cada vez denunciamos menos, un 9% de la víctimas habían denunciado a su agresor anteriormente”.


Y agregó: “Por supuesto faltan campañas de prevención, faltan que los medios de comunicación tengan pautas de los estados municipales, provinciales y nacionales para informar de qué hacer”.


Fuente:

https://agencia.farco.org.ar/2026/08/27/rosario-movilizacion-contra-los-femicidios-y-en-reclamo-de-la-emergencia-en-violencia-de-genero/

author: Rizomatica
title: Llenado del embalse de la central hidroeléctrica Los Lagos, un reconocimiento expreso de la violación a la debida diligencia por parte de Statkraft
content:
La confirmación de Statkraft refuerza la urgencia y la pertinencia de la queja presentada por el Aylla Rewe del Ngen Mapu Kintuantü ante las autoridades noruegas por posibles incumplimientos de las obligaciones de debida diligencia en materia de derechos humanos.


COMUNICADO DE PRENSA.


«Territorio del Pilmaykén, 26 de agosto de 2026. – Como Aylla Rewe del Ngen Mapu Kintuantü, recibimos con profunda preocupación la confirmación formal por parte de Statkraft de que concluyó el llenado del embalse del proyecto hidroeléctrico Los Lagos, en la cuenca del río Pilmaiquén.


Durante años hemos advertido públicamente sobre las consecuencias que este proyecto puede tener para nuestros derechos como pueblo Mapuche Williche, nuestra relación con el territorio, nuestra espiritualidad, nuestra cultura, nuestra memoriay nuestras formas de vida.


También es información pública que, dentro del territorio involucrado, existen espacios de profundo significado espiritual y cultural para nuestro pueblo y que en la zona se realizaron hallazgos arqueológicos y bioantropológicos de los cuales la empresa tenía conocimiento.


La empresa y las autoridades conocían estas preocupaciones antes de que se completara el llenado del embalse. Aun asi, la empresa decidió seguir adelante. La confirmación del llenado del embalse es una prueba flagrante de la violación a los estándares de debida diligencia corporativa en materia de derechos humanos y de la desatención a las voces y llamados reiterados de las comunidades.


Esta confirmación no resta importancia a las acciones legales que hemos impulsado. Por el contrario, confirma precisamente la urgencia y pertinencia de la queja que presentamos hace unas semanas ante la Autoridad de Consumo de Noruega, con el acompañamiento legal del Proyecto de Derechos Económicos, Sociales y Culturales (ProDESC) y de la Iniciativa para la Justicia Transnacional. (IJT), en la que solicitamos que se investigue si Statkraft cumplió adecuadamente con sus obligaciones de debida diligencia en materia de derechos humanos.


Para nosotros, trasladar elementos materiales no sustituye ni repara la relación espiritual, cultural y territorial de la que forman parte.


Como Aylla Rewe, hemos utilizado durante años las distintas vías legales e institucionales disponibles para exigir el respeto a nuestros derechos y que Statkraft cumpla con su obligación de debida diligencia.

Hemos participado e impulsado procesos relacionados con la consulta indígena, recurrido a instancias judiciales nacionales y presentado una queja ante el Punto Nacional de Contacto de Noruega por posibles incumplimientos de las Líneas Directrices de la OCDE para Empresas Multinacionales.


Ante la ausencia de una respuesta capaz de prevenir las afectaciones que veníamos advirtiendo, hace unas semanas nos vimos obligados a acudir nuevamente a las propias instituciones noruegas y presentar una queja al amparo de la Ley de Transparencia.

No llegamos a esta instancia como primera opción.

Llegamos después de años de utilizar mecanismos legales e institucionales para exigir que nuestros derechos fueran respetados antes de que el territorio fuera transformado.


Por eso, la confirmación del llenado del embalse vuelve la queja aún más urgente.

La debida diligencia en materia de derechos humanos no puede reducirse a cumplir procedimientos formales o a elaborar informes. Su función sustantiva es identificar los  riesgos, prevenir sus impactos, mitigarlos y actuar antes de que las afectaciones se materialicen.


Lo informado refuerza nuestra preocupación de que las advertencias de las comunidades y los riesgos para nuestros derechos no hayan sido atendidos de manera efectiva antes de que el proyecto avanzara y produjera transformaciones materiales en el territorio.


Ahora estamos documentando y verificando directamente el alcance de las afectaciones derivadas del llenado. Sin embargo, este proceso es sumamente complejo, pues, como es de público conocimiento, las comunidades no tienen acceso al sitio de construcción de la Central Los Lagos ni a sus zonas aledañas, ya que el área está resguardada por guardias privados de la empresa y por tanquetas apostadas en los caminos.


Esta situación confirma nuevamente que nuestro derecho de acceso a la información y a la participación en las decisiones que afectan nuestro territorio ha sido sistemáticamente vulnerado: ni las autoridades ni la empresa han garantizado su pleno ejercicio. Resulta especialmente grave que …

title: Rojhilat and Iranian organizations issue message on 4th anniversary of Jin, Jiyan, Azadî Revolution
content:
Ten civil society and labor organizations in Rojhilatê Kurdistan and Iran issued a written statement on the occasion of the fourth anniversary of the “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” Revolution.


The statement recalled that four years ago, Kurdish woman Jîna Emînî from the city of Saqiz in Rojhilatê Kurdistan was detained in Tehran on the grounds that she was not wearing a headscarf and was killed by the Iranian government. The statement said that Jîna Amini’s killing sparked a massive wave of social protest fueled by accumulated repression, discrimination, and corruption, adding: “People took to the streets, raising their voices against poverty, inequality, and colonialism.”


The statement noted that the slogan “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” quickly spread throughout the world and became an important turning point in the contemporary history of the peoples of Rojhilatê Kurdistan and Iran. It stated: “The Islamic Republic was unable to prevent society from moving forward through torture, repression, and executions.”


The statement emphasized that the “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” Revolution has spread into all areas of life and represents resistance against all forms of dictatorship, feudalism, and oppression.


At the end of the statement, all activists and organizations were called upon to celebrate the anniversary of the “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” Revolution and commemorate those who lost their lives in this struggle.

author: anred
title: El conurbano sur volvió a encontrarse: debate, organización y marcha en Monte Grande
content:
Fotos: Rocío Cisterna


En un contexto de profundización de la crisis económica y social, el sábado se realizó el 11° Encuentro Regional de Zona Sur. La jornada reunió a organizaciones y participantes del conurbano sur en una instancia de debate y convivencia. Salud, trabajo, educación, violencias y derechos humanos fueron los ejes de las rondas, que tuvieron una amplia participación. El encuentro finalizó con una marcha por el centro de Monte Grande.

Por ANRed 


Este sábado se llevó adelante el 11° Encuentro Regional de Zona Sur, una nueva jornada de participación, intercambio y organización que reunió a organizaciones transfeministas y participantes de distintos territorios del conurbano sur.


A lo largo del encuentro se desarrollaron cinco rondas de debate: Salud, Trabajo, Educación, Violencias y Derechos Humanos. Los espacios tuvieron una importante concurrencia y permitieron compartir experiencias, problemáticas y herramientas a partir de las distintas realidades territoriales.


En la ronda de Salud, una de las participantes destacó el valor del intercambio y de la construcción colectiva: “Estamos muy contentxs por este nuevo encuentro que nos reúne a todes para pensarnos desde el conurbano sur. Participé de la ronda de Salud y fue muy enriquecedor el intercambio que nos dimos para pensar en tejer redes para sostenernos en estos momentos de profundización de las crisis”.


“Es muy importante saber que nos tenemos y que podemos confiar en nuestras organizaciones transfeministas”, agregó.


Además de las rondas, la jornada estuvo atravesada por una gran convivencia entre quienes participaron del encuentro, generando un espacio para compartir experiencias y fortalecer los vínculos entre organizaciones y territorios.


 


Una marcha por Monte Grande


Como cierre de la jornada, se realizó una marcha que comenzó en el Instituto Superior de Formación Docente N°35 y recorrió distintos puntos de Monte Grande.


Una de las primeras paradas fue el Hospital Santamarina, donde las organizaciones feministas denunciaron las presiones ejercidas por grupos antiderechos para impedir que se garantice el acceso a la interrupción voluntaria del embarazo, derecho contemplado por la Ley 27.610 de Acceso a la Interrupción Voluntaria del Embarazo.


La movilización continuó hasta la Comisaría Nro 1, donde se realizó una intervención artística. En la puerta de la dependencia policial fueron arrojadas cajas de pizza con distintas leyendas, entre ellas “Ustedes tienen que cuidarnos”, en referencia a la falta de respuestas frente a las agresiones machistas y las situaciones de violencia que atraviesan mujeres, travestis, lesbianas y personas no binarias.


La marcha continuó por la Municipalidad de Esteban Echeverría y la iglesia, para finalizar en la Plaza de Monte Grande, donde se realizó el cierre de la jornada.


Una de las participantes destacó el significado del encuentro y su dimensión colectiva: “Venir a los encuentros te llena de alegría, que no es poco en estos momentos de individualismo y sufrimiento colectivo. Saber que hay muches en diferentes lugares haciendo lo posible e imposible para mejorar nuestra calidad de vida estimula a salir de la queja y ponernos a trabajar en comunidad”.


“Celebro haber participado de este evento, que es único e importante en el conurbano sur”, agregó.


De esta manera, el 11° Encuentro Regional de Zona Sur combinó debate, intercambio y movilización, fortaleciendo un espacio de articulación entre organizaciones y territorios del conurbano sur..
