author: Publicación Abierta
title: Quirno afirmó que las medidas sobre Malvinas no tuvieron nada que ver con el Mundial ni Trump
content:
Quirno aseguró que la estrategia oficial comenzó a diseñarse varios meses atrás


El canciller Pablo Quirno junto al presidente Javier Milei. Presidencia


Mario Hernandez


El canciller Pablo Quirno rechazó que las recientes medidas del Gobierno de Javier Milei por las Islas Malvinas hayan surgido a partir de la bandera exhibida durante el Mundial 2026 o de las declaraciones del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump.


A través de una publicación en sus redes sociales, el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores, Comercio Internacional y Culto defendió el trabajo realizado de manera conjunta con el Ministerio de Defensa, encabezado por Carlos Presti, y aseguró que existe una estrategia integrada para Malvinas y el Atlántico Sur.


Quirno salió así al cruce de las versiones que relacionaron las últimas decisiones adoptadas por la Casa Rosada con episodios recientes vinculados al reclamo de soberanía argentino. “Cuando dicen que fue la bandera del Mundial o las declaraciones del presidente Trump para minimizar el trabajo realizado durante meses para llegar a articular una estrategia integrada de defensa de nuestros intereses en Malvinas y el Atlántico Sur…”, escribió el canciller.


En su publicación, Quirno citó un mensaje de Presti referido a una reunión realizada en mayo en la Base Naval Integrada de Tierra del Fuego, con el objetivo de remarcar que la planificación comenzó meses antes de los acontecimientos que ahora quedaron en el centro de la discusión.


Las declaraciones del canciller se produjeron después de la cadena nacional de Javier Milei, en la que el Presidente anunció nuevas medidas contra las compañías que participen de actividades hidrocarburíferas en las Islas Malvinas sin autorización argentina. En ese contexto, Quirno lanzó una fuerte advertencia a unas 180 empresas vinculadas directa o indirectamente con la explotación de hidrocarburos en el archipiélago.


El Gobierno pretende que esas compañías deban optar entre continuar con sus operaciones relacionadas con Malvinas y exponerse a sanciones por parte del Estado argentino, o abandonar su participación en esos proyectos.


Durante su exposición en la 47.ª Convención Anual del Instituto Argentino de Ejecutivos de Finanzas (IAEF), el canciller explicó que la estrategia no apunta únicamente a las petroleras que desarrollen actividades en las islas, sino también a las empresas que les proporcionen diferentes tipos de servicios. El objetivo, según detalló, es ampliar el alcance de las sanciones a toda la estructura que permite desarrollar los proyectos hidrocarburíferos.


 


Qué empresas podrían ser sancionadas por operar en Malvinas


Quirno sostuvo que el nuevo decreto reglamentario busca, además, acelerar los procedimientos para aplicar sanciones contra las compañías involucradas. “Un decreto reglamentario para darle celeridad a las sanciones a las compañías que operen en Malvinas, las compañías que operen en Malvinas más sus proveedores de servicios petroleros, de servicios financieros, de servicio de seguro, etc.”, explicó.


El Gobierno busca ahora avanzar con la aplicación de las nuevas herramientas para presionar a las compañías extranjeras involucradas en la explotación de hidrocarburos en Malvinas y el Atlántico Sur, en el marco del reclamo argentino de soberanía sobre el archipiélago.


 


SLB, ex Schlumberger, Halliburton y Baker Hughes anunciaron que acatarían las advertencias argentinas


 


Primero había sido SLB, la ex Schlumberger, la mayor proveedora de servicios petroleros del mundo, anunciando que acataría las advertencias argentinas y no tendría negocios con las empresas del proyecto petrolero ‘Sea Lion’ en Malvinas. Y horas más tarde las estadounidenses Halliburton y Baker Hughes asumieron similar compromiso, ratificando que “respetan la soberanía argentina” en las islas y no harán trabajos con los kelpers.


Los pronunciamientos de las tres empresas fueron celebrados por YPF, que destacó la continuidad de su actividad en la Argentina.


SLB había informado que “en atención a lo establecido por el Decreto 868/26 del Poder Ejecutivo Nacional, no está participando ni tiene previsto participar en procesos de licitación que tengan por objeto la prestación de servicios para proyectos hidrocarburíferos en las Islas Malvinas, así como en los espacios marítimos circundantes”. La compañía reafirmó además “su compromiso con el cumplimiento de las normas vigentes”.

title: Panorama sindical: La película que ven los trabajadores es de terror
content:
Boletín de informaciones sindicales actualizado al 7.9.2026


Foto. Maia Pauro


La película que ven los trabajadores es de terror


Mario Hernandez


 


Fate cumplió 90 días de lucha. Trabajadores de Arsat contra congelamiento salarial y desguace. Despiden delegada del Garrahan. 6t

a. semana de paro docente en T. del Fuego.

Actos por despidos en Will Der. Paro general petrolero en Santa Cruz y metalúrgico en Tierra del Fuego. ATE rechazó propuesta salarial. Paro del personal civil de las FF AA. Paro en aeropuertos. Causa por “asociación ilícita” contra trabajadores del Subte. Carrefour y Autofarma despiden en Río Gallegos (Santa Cruz). Movilización y paro docente en PBA. Muere en Corrientes líder contra cierre de Alal. Quiebra fábrica en Córdoba. Y la única fábrica de aviones al borde del concurso. Podría concluir el conflicto en la Justicia cordobesa. Trabajadores no médicos de Coseme (Córdoba) de paro. Suspensiones en Pauny. El Hípermercado Libertad cierra en Mendoza y Godoy Cruz. Cierran sucursales de Musimundo en Corrientes y el Nordeste. Cierre definitivo de Clan Issime en La Plata, Pampa Energía, Fábrica Argentina de Porcelana Armanino y Granja Tres Arroyos Capitán Sarmiento. Universitarios rechazan aumento salarial. Paro de los judiciales porteños.


 


Los trabajadores de FATE realizaron un festival en Plaza de Mayo


A seis meses del cierre de FATE, realizaron un festival en Plaza de Mayo para insistir en la continuidad de los puestos de trabajo. Capturas de Video


A más de seis meses de la decisión del empresario Javier Madanes Quintanilla de cerrar las puertas de la fábrica de neumáticos FATE y dejar a 

920 trabajadores en la calle

, los trabajadores despedidos junto con el Sindicato Único de Trabajadores del Neumático (Sutna) realizaron un 

festival en Plaza de Mayo 

para insistir en que se garantice la continuidad de los puestos de trabajo, poner fin al lock out empresarial y lograr la 

reapertura de la planta

.


Los trabajadores del neumático fueron acompañados en Plaza de Mayo por gremios como Suteba Tigre, GPS-Aerolíneas y distintos agrupamientos de jubilados y jubiladas en un festival que contó con la participación de las bandas Horcas y Las Manos de Filippi.


“Hay que 

confiar en la fuerza de los trabajadores

, por eso es indispensable salir a la calle, llamar a la coordinación de todos los sectores y dar una pelea denunciando el lock out y por la reapertura de la planta”, sostuvo, en Plaza de Mayo, el operario Sebastián Tesoro, uno de los que sostiene la 

ocupación pacífica dentro de la empresa de Madanes Quintanilla

.


“

Estamos en el acampe, dentro de la fábrica, sosteniendo la pelea por los puestos de trabajo

. Es importante la confianza en nuestra propia fuerza. Si la Justicia no nos da la razón, si la Legislatura no quiere atender nuestro reclamo, tenemos que tomarlo los trabajadores en nuestras manos”, sostuvo .


Entre los 920 trabajadores despedidos en febrero pasado, cuando algunos de ellos regresaban de vacaciones, estaba Cristian, quien trabajó 17 años en la empresa y después de meses consiguió otro empleo como repartidor de agua. “

Yo tengo fe en que vamos a lograr que la fábrica vuelva a abrir

, pero no nos podemos quedar de brazos cruzados, la vida me enseñó a trabajar”, comentaba en diálogo con 

C5N

.


Cristian relató lo que significó 

perder todos los beneficios de estar con un empleo en blanco

, entre ellos una obra social para toda su familia, y lamentó la actitud de la empresa Madanes Quintanilla: “Da bronca que una fábrica como esta haga un lock out patronal y cierre por interés propio, porque son tipos muy poderosos, nuestros salarios son migajas para ellos”.


Los trabajadores de Fate 

enfrentan procesamientos por “usurpación” 

por mantener la ocupación de la fábrica en resguardo de la maquinaria y las 

más de 50 mil cubiertas que quedaron sin vender en stock

. También consiguieron fallos favorables de la justicia en contra de la orden de desalojo y por el reconocimiento de sus salarios caídos. En tanto, 

esperan que el parlamento bonaerense trate un proyecto de ley a favor de la ocupación temporal de la planta.


Los trabajadores del Sutna, encabezado por Alejandro Crespo, sostienen que Fate no era cualquier fábrica, sino

 la única fabricante de neumáticos para camiones y colectivos del país

, por lo que su cierre también implica una cuestión de soberanía para la logística del país.


En el reclamo que sostienen hace más de seis meses …

author: Amanda Audi
title: Quem são os “coaches” de Michelle Bolsonaro
content:
Investigamos o que importa para os brasileiros além do que passa na campanha eleitoral. Leia mais reportagens como essa clicando

aqui

.


Michelle Bolsonaro mudou.

Sua imagem migrou de uma primeira-dama tímida e apagada para uma das lideranças políticas mais influentes do país

 – mesmo disputando seu primeiro cargo eletivo só agora, aos 44 anos, ao Senado. Uma das explicações para essa mudança, segundo pastores e especialistas em religião ouvidos pela

Agência Pública

, foram as pessoas de quem

ela se cercou: lideranças evangélicas que acreditam que os cristãos devem participar – se não dominar – todas as esferas da sociedade, incluindo o governo, para subordinar o Estado aos valores bíblicos – a chamada teologia do domínio.


Para esses grupos, é dever do cristão ocupar cargos de poder para “libertar” os espaços da influência do diabo. Vale para política, educação, família, religião, mídia, entretenimento e negócios – considerados os “sete montes de influência”. Esse entendimento alcança várias das lideranças evangélicas mais conhecidas do Brasil hoje.

Boa parte delas é do círculo pessoal de Michelle, consideradas por ela seus conselheiros espirituais, e que moldaram a sua maneira de ver o mundo. 


De primeira-dama discreta a liderança política: Michelle Bolsonaro se cercou de líderes ligados à teologia do domínio atual


Três episódios ocorridos entre as eleições de 2018 e 2026 ajudam a ilustrar como ela passou a transitar entre esses dois polos – religião e política – e cravar o seu espaço no pólo conservador com apoio dos adeptos mais ferrenhos da teologia do domínio, e que podem ter peso para a candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro. 


Pouco antes das eleições de 2018, o pastor José Wellington Bezerra, um dos principais líderes da Assembleia de Deus no Brasil, visitou a casa de Bolsonaro, então postulante à Presidência. “De todos os candidatos, o único que fala o idioma do evangélico é Bolsonaro”, ele disse, na época. A frase costuma ser lembrada por incutir uma certa contradição: apesar de receber apoio massivo do público evangélico, Bolsonaro se declara católico. Ainda pouco conhecida do público, Michelle não apareceu nas fotos divulgadas do dia.


Na campanha de 2022, a equipe de Bolsonaro percebeu que ela poderia ser uma peça-chave para acessar mulheres evangélicas, um dos públicos mais reticentes com o bolsonarismo. A partir de agosto daquele ano, ela se tornou quase onipresente nos eventos da campanha.

 Em longas falas parecidas com sermões de igreja, ela declarava que o marido era um “escolhido de Deus” e que a sua reeleição tinha um “propósito de libertação” da nação. 


Foi o ponto decisivo para a entrada de Michelle na política, galgando espaço para o seu projeto mais ambicioso: o PL Mulher, ala do partido que promove encontros entre mulheres conservadoras

 – onde se discute política ao mesmo tempo em que se fala de religião, família, cuidado e outros assuntos considerados femininos (não feministas). Sob a batuta de Michelle, o PL Mulher se espalhou por todos os estados como uma versão brasileira dos encontros de mulheres republicanas dos Estados Unidos.


Desde 2022, Michelle Bolsonaro se tornou uma das principais pontes entre o bolsonarismo e o eleitorado evangélico


Dois dias depois do primeiro turno, quando o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva já demonstrava vantagem sobre Bolsonaro, o casal Bolsonaro retribuiu a visita de José Wellington na eleição anterior no megatemplo que ele preside, em São Paulo. O pastor pediu abertamente votos para o capitão. Mas, desta vez, Michelle estava no púlpito, e discursou enquanto o marido chorava. A primeira-dama comparou a disputa eleitoral a uma batalha da “luz contra as trevas” e cobrou a igreja a ter uma posição no segundo turno. “A gente precisa se voltar ao Senhor. A igreja precisa se posicionar, a igreja precisa aprender”, disse ela.


Já em 2026, com Bolsonaro em prisão domiciliar, seu filho Flávio foi o escolhido pelo patriarca para disputar a presidência. Com

dificuldades para ter o mesmo apoio

 recebido pelo pai entre os evangélicos, o filho 01 decidiu fazer um tour por várias denominações – e começou justamente pela igreja do pastor José Wellington, que lhe ofereceu a mesma simpatia. “Que o Senhor o leve para ser presidente da nossa nação” disse na ocasião, enquanto ungia o senador. 


Senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) durante encontro com lideranças evangélicas na Assembleia de Deus, Ministério de Belém


Ele não contava, porém, que o estopim …

author: Mosha Folger
title: New Brunswick charity sends sea can of food to Igloolik
content:
A charity in New Brunswick sent enough food to fill a sealift container — about $50,000 worth — to Igloolik late last month.


A Tapestry of Kindness is run by husband and wife Rick Maher and Linda Maher and funded by their friend Charlie Cahill, all of whom are originally from St. John’s, N.L., and have known each other since university. They sent the bounty to St. Stephen Church Rev. Zbigniew Halemba.


Halemba said he recruited 20 volunteers, including students and teachers, to move the food from the container to the church and from there had given out approximately 200 food hampers as of Aug. 30 the approximately 2,000 people who live in Igloolik.


Halemba, who moved to Canada from Poland in 2021 and four months ago left Naujaat for Igloolik, said distributing such a large donation helped acquaint him with Igloolik residents.


“Many of them didn’t know me and they were also coming to me and telling me this is a first time that we have something like this,” he said.


“I was really happy to hear that I can do something good…. It takes time that people can trust you, that people can come to you.”


Rick Maher and Linda Maher began working on what would eventually become A Tapestry of Kindness in January 2025. The charity is registered in Saint John, N.B., where the Mahers now live.


The food was purchased in Quebec, Rich Maher said, near where the sealift cargo ships depart for Nunavut communities. He bought several items in bulk, including peanut butter, macaroni pasta, tomato sauce, tea, sugar, cereal, and canned corn and peas.


He said he’s hoping to donate to two Nunavut communities a year, and is working to secure grant funding from Nutrition North Canada to cover part of the transportation costs. The charity has also made a

donation

 of food to Gjoa Haven in September 2025.


“The transportation cost of each sea can is approximately $12,000,” Maher said.


“We have an active grant application with Nutrition North which will help cover some transportation costs associated with this year’s shipments. Those funds are forthcoming and will contribute to next year’s efforts.”


Halemba said that, besides feeding the community, he sees another meaningful outcome from the donation.


“I believe that food may be some kind of thing that connects us, because we know that in the past many times Anglicans and Catholics were

fighting

, and sometimes you can even still feel it in some communities,” Halemba said.


“I believe that those things, like giving away food, sharing, or praying together, that we like somehow repair something that was a little bit broken in the past.”

title: Selçuk Mızraklı released from prison
content:
Selçuk Mızraklı, former Co-Mayor of Diyarbakır Metropolitan Municipality, was released after nearly seven years of imprisonment. He had been held in the same cell with Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP) former Co-Chair Selahattin Demirtaş for the past four and a half years.


Mızraklı left the Edirne High-Security Closed Prison after the necessary procedures were completed. He was welcomed outside the prison by his family and a large crowd.


People who had gathered outside the prison early in the morning unfurled banners reading: “Welcome, Selçuk Mızraklı,” “May your freedom be blessed, comrade,” “Freedom cannot be partial — freedom for Demirtaş,” and “Mızraklı’s freedom is our joy; Demirtaş’s imprisonment is our anger.”


Politician and doctor Selçuk Mızraklı was arrested in October 2019 while serving as the Co-Mayor of Diyarbakır Metropolitan Municipality and was replaced by a state-appointed trustee five months after his election. He had been imprisoned since.

title: Selçuk Mızraklı: The process needs to be made transparent
content:
Selçuk Mızraklı, former Co-Mayor of Diyarbakır Metropolitan Municipality, was released from Edirne F-Type High-Security Closed Prison after nearly seven years. He was welcomed outside the prison by his family, relatives and representatives of political parties.


Speaking briefly to journalists, Mızraklı said that the rule of law and democracy in Turkey had been seriously eroded since 2015, stressing that the process in the new period needs to be made transparent so that society can see the way forward.


‘What we lost is the rule of law and democracy’


Mızraklı pointed out that Turkey is going through a critical period. According to the politician, the process must be carried out carefully, diligently and swiftly, taking into account the possibility of provocations from outside.


Describing the period since 2015 as one in which “lawlessness reached its peak,” Mızraklı said that democratic values had also been eroded. “They say you look for what you have lost where you lost it. I will not go into an assessment of the past century, but the defining feature of the period since 2015 has been lawlessness — stepping outside the rule of law (…) What we lost is the rule of law. The second thing we lost is democracy,” he stated.


‘Steps are needed to build trust in society’


Pointing to the talk of a new climate of peace in Turkey, Mızraklı remarked that this does not simply mean an end to conflict, but requires a process of confronting the past and addressing the harm that has been done.


Stating that steps are needed to build trust in society if peace is to become lasting, he said, “The most important aspect of this is transparency.”


“As political actors, society and the peoples of Turkey, we want to be able to see the path ahead. For that to happen, the process needs to be made transparent and access to information needs to be expanded,” Mızraklı said.


Message from Demirtaş


Mızraklı also emphasized the need for the release of Selahattin Demirtaş, whose name has become closely associated with Edirne Prison. Relaying the message Demirtaş gave him as he was leaving, Mızraklı quoted his demand as “democracy, peace and a resolution, no matter what.”


Mızraklı said that free and unrestricted talks should be held with all political actors, including Demirtaş and Abdullah Öcalan, and called on journalists to support efforts in this direction.


Stressing that the freedom of those released from prison must be fully realized, Mızraklı said he was not afraid of returning to Edirne Prison, but that next time he hoped to come back to bring out his friends still inside, particularly Demirtaş.


Doctor, human rights advocate and politician


Adnan Selçuk Mızraklı worked as a physician in various hospitals in Amed from 1991 onward. From 2008 to 2010, he served as chair of the Amed Medical Chamber and held various other positions within the organization over many years. Mızraklı was also active in the fields of social solidarity and human rights.


He served as chair of the Sarmaşık Association for Combating Poverty and Sustainable Development, founded in 2006 by local authorities and numerous civil society organizations. The association provided thousands of low-income families with food as well as healthcare and educational support. In 2011, he was among the founders of the Mesopotamia Foundation, which advocates, among other things, for multilingual education.


Removed from office and replaced by a state-appointed trustee


In the 2018 parliamentary elections, Mızraklı was elected to the Turkish Parliament as an MP for Amed representing the Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP). In the local elections held on March 31, 2019, he ran for Co-Mayor of Amed Metropolitan Municipality and won the election.


Only a few months later, on August 19, 2019, Turkey’s Ministry of Interior removed Mızraklı from office and replaced him with a state-appointed trustee.


On the day of his removal from office, when Mızraklı was asked to formally acknowledge the Interior Ministry’s decision at the municipal building, he refused to sign it. Instead, he wrote on the notification document: “On behalf of the people who entrusted me with this mandate, I would consider it dishonorable to sign this.”


He subsequently took part in days-long protests outside the municipal building against the appointment of the state trustee and also resisted police interventions against the gatherings. In October 2019, Mızraklı was detained and remanded in custody on …

title: YPG commemorates Commander Yaşar Berçelan
content:
The People’s Defense Units (YPG) announced the death of their commander Yaşar Berçelan. According to a statement issued by the YPG Press Office on Monday, the revolutionary was martyred on November 13, 2024, in an airstrike by the Turkish state on the northern Syrian city of Aleppo.


Yaşar Berçelan, whose real name was Aydın Elmas, was from Hakkari. According to the YPG, he had spent many years as a guerrilla fighter in the mountains of Kurdistan before going to Rojava. He reportedly played a particularly important role in the resistance against the “Islamic State” (ISIS) terrorist organization in Shengal and Rojava.


Commander during the resistance in Shengal


When ISIS attacked the Shengal region in August 2014, Berçelan, together with other fighters, went to Rojava to take part in the defense against the genocide of the Yazidi community. As a YPG and YPJ commander, he played a key role in opening the humanitarian corridor through which tens of thousands of Yazidis were rescued from the Shengal Mountains.


According to the YPG, Berçelan subsequently served as a regional commander, coordinating the fighting on the Rabia-Til Kocher and Jazaa fronts.


“When necessary, he himself took his place on the front lines as a fighter and stood alongside his comrades with great determination throughout this historic process,” the obituary stated. Berçelan also took part in further offensives against ISIS. The YPG cited Til Hemîs, Til Berak, Hol, southern Hesekê and Manbij, where he reportedly served as a coordinator of military operations.


“A source of confidence and determination”


The YPG paid tribute to Berçelan as an experienced commander who placed great importance on the training of fighters during the Rojava Revolution. According to the statement, he passed on the experience he had accumulated over many years in the Kurdish freedom struggle and played a particularly important role in the field of military tactics.


“Comrade Yaşar was always a source of confidence, enthusiasm and determination among our forces,” the YPG stated. From the mountains of Kurdistan to Shengal and Rojava, the statement said, he embodied his deep connection to his home region of Botan. His comrades knew him as a humble, self-sacrificing person with a deep connection to nature.


“Throughout his life, Yaşar Berçelan always sought to serve his people even more,” the statement continued. “He loved his people and devoted all his strength to serving them. He treated everyone with respect. From elderly mothers to children in the cradle, every person was a reason for him to remain committed to the struggle. We commemorate him with love and respect.”

title: Aydın: What kind of process is this if they ransack our home while we are mourning?
content:
While Abdullah Aydın was mourning his brother Fatih Aydın and his cousin Vedat Aydın, four plainclothes men forcibly entered his home in Istanbul. According to Aydın, the men identified themselves as representatives of the state, searched the apartment, spat on a photograph of his fallen brother and threw it to the floor. “What kind of process is this if they ransack our home while we are mourning? Can there be a resolution process, can there be peace under such circumstances?” Aydın asked in an interview with ANF.


Only a few weeks earlier, Aydın had learned that his brother Fatih Aydın (Agir Mêrdîn) and his cousin Vedat Aydın (Piling Barman) had lost their lives in the Kurdish freedom struggle. Fatih Aydın joined the guerrilla ranks in 2013 after spending six months in prison. For years, his family received no news from him. It was only when the names of those who had lost their lives were announced that the family learned he had died in 2021.


“We were like twins”


Abdullah Aydın received condolences for his brother in Ümraniye. He said that with his brother’s death, a part of him had been left incomplete. Fatih was only a year older and was the sibling he had been closest to.


“We were born in the village of Yeşilalan in Savur, Mardin and grew up together. We were in the same class and have many wonderful memories together. He always protected me. When I was a child, I would get into fights with other children, they would beat me up, and then he would come and beat them up,” Aydın recalled.


He described his brother as very emotional and straightforward: “He would get angry very quickly, but calm down just as quickly. Whatever was on his mind, he would say it directly to your face. He was always cleaning up after me. We were always together; we were like twins. It was only after we moved to Istanbul that our paths slowly began to diverge.”


Pressure over speaking Kurdish at school


Although their generation was no longer subjected to state repression to the same extent as previous generations, Aydın said they had experienced racism at school.


“The teacher treated us as if we were foreigners. Whenever we spoke our mother tongue, Kurdish, he tried to silence us and constantly pressured us by saying, ‘Speak Turkish.’ We could never accept that. We questioned this racism deeply. My brother Fatih, in particular, reflected on it intensely. Later, this developed into a broader questioning of the entire system.”


“Three days earlier, I saw him in a dream”


The family had already lost their father in 2000, while their mother died of stomach cancer in 2008. The family then moved to Istanbul. Abdullah Aydın was 15 at the time, and his brother Fatih followed a year later. While Abdullah worked, Fatih continued his education and moved to Kars to study logistics. After two years, he returned to Istanbul.


“He said, ‘I can’t stand this system here anymore.’ After that, he became increasingly politically active. In 2013, he was arrested and spent six months in prison. Two months after his release, he went to the mountains.”


From then on, the family heard nothing from him for years. It was only a few weeks ago, when the identities of those who had lost their lives were announced, that they learned Fatih had died in 2021.


“Three days before I received the news of his death, I saw him in a dream. Fatih said to me, ‘Come and pick me up from the border. I’m going home.’ Three days later, the news of his death came.”


“We are the state”


After learning of the deaths of Fatih Aydın and Vedat Aydın, Abdullah Aydın sent some members of his family to their home region for the mourning ceremony and returned to the apartment in Ümraniye. He said the incident occurred there on August 22.


“About 15 minutes after I got home, the doorbell rang. Four men in plain clothes were standing outside. When I asked who they were, one of them immediately struck me in the chest and said, ‘We are the state.’ Then they forced their way into the apartment.”


According to Aydın, the identification cards shown to him by the men bore the words “Undersecretariat of the National Intelligence Organization” (MİT). When he asked what they wanted from him, they replied: “We are the state; we do whatever we want.”


The men then ransacked the apartment. One of them approached a photograph of Fatih Aydın that was standing on a dresser. “He spat on it and threw it to the floor. He was about to step on it when I picked up the photograph and put it …

title: Îkra Avciya ku ji bo tûndkariya li dijî jinan porê xwe hûnandibû ji fermanberiyê hat derxistin
content:
Li Rojavayê jinekê Kurd, piştî hat kuştin keziyê wê yê hûnandî ji aliyê endamekî komek çekdar ve hatibû birîn. Perestar Îkra Avciya ku li Kocaeliyê dixebitî jî bi hûnandina porê xwe li dijî vê yekê bertek nîşan dabû.


Îkra Avciyê bi rêya hesabê xwe yê medyaya civakî da zanîn ku ew piştî biryara Lijneya Bilind a Dîsîplînê ya Wezareta Tenduristiyê ji erkê xwe hatiye derxistin.


Avciyê metna biryarê parve kir û got:


"Min hêvî dikir ku ev biryara şaş were betalkirin. Îro ji min re hat ragihandin ku ji karê memûriyetê hatime derxistin."


Li gorî agahiyên hatine bidestxistin, dosyeya ku ji aliyê Birêvebiriya Giştî ya Xizmetên Kargêriyê ya Wezareta Tenduristiyê ve li ser serlêdana Birêvebiriya Tenduristiyê ya Kocaeliyê hatibû amadekirin, li Lijneya Bilind a Dîsîplînê ya Wezaretê gihîşt biryara dawî.


Li gorî biryara ku li civîna 19ê Tebaxa 2026an hatiye girtin, çalakiya Avciyê di çarçoveya xala 125an a Qanûna Karmendên Sîvîl a Hejmar 657 de hatiye nirxandin.


Lijneyê doz bi angaşta hûnandina keziyê ango ji ber "têkbirina aramî û rêziknameya xebata saziyan a ji bo armancên îdeolojîk an siyasî" bi cezayê "derxistina ji karê xizmeta sîvîl" bi dawî kir. Di agahdarnameyê de hat destnîşankirin ku Avci dikare li dijî vê biryarê serî li dadgeha kargêriyê bide.


Çi bûbû?


Di dema êrişên komên çekdar ên girêdayî Birêvebiriya Şamê yên li Rojavayê de, endamekî komeke çekdar Ramî Yûsif Deheş (Ramî Haşimî) keziya şervaneke jin a ku canê xwe ji dest dabû jêkiribû.


Ramî Yûsif Deheş vîdeoya vê yekê belav kiribû û ev bûyerê di nava raya giştî de bû sedema nîşandana nerazîbûneke mezin.


Piştî vê yekê jinan li ser medyaya civakî porên xwe hûnabûn û kampanyayeke piştgiriyê dabû destpêkirin. Ji siyasetmedaran heta rojnamegeran, ji hunermendan heta xebatkarên tenduristiyê gelek kesan piştgirî dabû kampanyayê.


Îkra Avciya ku li nexweşxaneyeke Kocaeliyê dixebitî, piştî posta xwe ya piştgiriyê li ser medyaya civakî bûbû hedefa nijadperestên Tirk. Ew pişt re bi îdiaya "propagandaya rêxistinê" hatibû desteserkirin.


Birêvebiriya Tenduristiyê ya Bajarê Kocaeliyê ragihandibû ku li ser Îlra Avciyê him lêpirsîna edlî him jî ya îdarî hatiye destpêkirin.


(AY)

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Netanyahu ‘Was Warned Ahead of October 7 but Failed to Act’
content:
Benjamin Netanyahu received a direct warning that Hamas was planning a major attack in the run-up to 7 October 2023 but failed to act,

an Israeli newspaper has alleged

.


The investigation, published by Haaretz on Tuesday, claims that UAE president Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed told the Israeli prime minister by phone that the armed group was “preparing for a major event”.


Netanyahu did not tell intelligence and military leaders about the conversation, according to the report, which cites unnamed senior foreign sources and a close adviser to bin Zayed who was present on the call.


Israeli intelligence officials were, however, made aware of Hamas’ plans for an attack, according to the investigation: then-Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar warned Israel himself via an intermediary.


Netanyahu’s office called the claim an “absolute lie” and denied that he had a call with the Emirati leader around that time or received any warning. The office of bin Zayed did not respond to a request for comment from Haaretz.


After growing frustrated with stalled negotiations aimed at lifting Israel’s illegal blockade on Gaza, Sinwar reportedly told the mediator to “convey a message” to the Israeli side. He said: “I am preparing the mother of all surprises. A terrifying operation. Something extraordinary.”


On 15 September, both the mediator and bin Zayed’s advisor relayed the message to Shin Bet, Israel’s internal intelligence service, the report alleges. Ex-Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar and ex-IDF chief of staff Herzl Halevi said they were not informed of a warning from the president of the UAE.


An anonymous intelligence official quoted by Haaretz speculated that Sinwar sent the warning to “pressure” Israel into reaching a deal, or else as a tactic to assess the readiness of the Israel Defense Forces.


It has

previously been reported

 that Egyptian officials

warned Israel

just days before 7 October that “something catastrophic” was about to happen.


In the wake of the attacks, Haaretz reports, Hamas was willing to unconditionally release all civilian captives, or at least all those below the age of 18 and over 50. Further offers followed, but Netanyahu’s government refused to engage, sources said.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: ‘The theft is blatant’: Nunavut AI ‘correspondent’ regurgitates northern stories
content:
Leah Qammaniq, an Inuk journalist raised in the North, understands first-hand the issues that she reports on in Nunavut. She covers Inuit self-governance, food security and, generally, daily life in the territory. According to her publisher, her writing is “warm, precise, and deeply local.”


This is an AI-generated image of Leah Qammaniq, Nunavut’s new AI ‘correspondent.’ She is not a real person. (Graphic courtesy of We-News)


She also isn’t real.


Qammaniq is an “AI correspondent” for

We-News.com

, a website that presents itself as a news outlet but uses 121 AI “journalists” to repackage and republish work from real media, across the world.


If Qammaniq’s reporting comes across as deeply local, it’s because it is. The reporting belongs to northern media such as CBC North, Nunavut News and Nunatsiaq News.


“As a journalist, it frankly disgusts me to see the public’s right to know being manipulated by algorithms and artificial intelligence,” said Brent Jolly, president of the Canadian Association of Journalists, in an interview.

“It frustrates me to no end that this is something that the public doesn’t seem to realize, and that we’re not asking more questions about what’s happening and how we can address this.”


Unlike a real newsroom, fake ones can’t be held accountable the same way if they publish false information, Jolly said.


In We-News’s case, it’s unclear to what extent humans review its content. Its website claims that the outlet delivers “essential stories without sacrificing reliability” and that every story “is confirmed by multiple sources before publication.”


When Nunatsiaq News attempted to use the contact email on its website, the email bounced back.


We-News is owned by Hong Kong-based company AZ Medias Ltd, its publisher is David Dragesco, and the website’s hosting provider is located in France.


Nunatsiaq News attempted to get in touch with someone named David Dragesco, a search-engine optimization expert whose business website DiscoReady is also published by AZ Medias Ltd., but did not receive a response.


“The theft is blatant and it’s happening on an industrial scale,” said Paul Deegan, president of News Media Canada, which represents print and digital news publishers throughout the country.


Right now, the only way newsrooms can fight back against their copyrighted material being stolen is a lawsuit, he said, which isn’t realistic. Many publishers can’t afford to litigate, and tracking down offenders across borders to serve them with legal documents is difficult.


Even if a newsroom succeeds in getting one website shut down, Jolly added, new ones can always be created.


“It’s a game of whack-a-mole,” he said.


News Media Canada has asked that Canada’s Copyright Act not be amended to make exceptions for text and data mining, a change Google has lobbied for in AI training.


Jolly and Deegan said they were disappointed to see the subject of copyright omitted from Canada’s new AI strategy, released by the Liberal government earlier this summer. The strategy includes more than $2 billion in funding to increase the country’s AI capacity. 


Nunatsiaq News asked Evan Solomon, Canada’s minister of artificial intelligence, what his position was on AI republishing of copyrighted materials from newsrooms, but did not receive an answer. Culture Minister Marc Miller, who co-hosted the country’s first national summit on artificial intelligence alongside Solomon, didn’t state his position on the matter either.


“The government remains focused on helping journalists, writers and artists create and share the work that informs Canadians and tells our stories,” wrote David Larose, a spokesperson for the minister, noting an AI and cultural advisory council has been established to provide advice to government in response to the impacts AI is having on the cultural sector.


Ahmed Al-Rawi is an associate professor at Simon Fraser University, in B.C., and the lead on the Disinformation Project, a research institute that studies fake news. In an interview, he said that, while some websites like We-News openly state they use AI, that doesn’t mean they aren’t also trying to mislead the public into believing they’re reading real journalists.


“The problem is that they actually have a picture of the alleged author of each news article, and that picture is a human, so it’s confusing,” he said. “One has to read the fine lines in order to figure it out.”


These websites might just have ad revenue in …

author: Unknown
title: Rencontre avec Caroline Knecht et Sandra Lucbert autour du livre Ainsi la Cour décide
content:
Jeudi 10 septembre à 19h30 à la librairie le Monte en l'air, Caroline Knecht discutera avec Zoé Carle de son livre Ainsi la Cour décide, premier titre du label Catabase dirigé par Sandra Lucbert.


Le livre propose le démontage d'une institution : la Cour nationale du droit d'asile – et des politiques qu'elle fait exister. Le texte procède par courts chapitres où se mêlent narration et collage.


Cette nouvelle collection des éditions La Découverte se positionne comme label littéraire politique. Chaque texte proposera un dispositif formel spécifique, pensé en adéquation avec l'objet social dont il se saisit.


RESUME

 :


Chaque jour, à la Cour nationale du droit d'asile, des craintes bruissent par milliers, et chaque jour, à la Cour nationale du droit d'asile, des juges en jugent le bien-fondé. Dévisagent les exils. Accordent le refuge à une petite minorité. On dit qu'ils protègent.


Mais qui protègent-ils, au juste

 

?


Après avoir (pas tout à fait bien) étudié le droit, Caroline Knecht se tourne (un temps) vers l'anthropologie puis (vraiment) vers la littérature pour éplucher les langues et façons juridiques - et autres espaces de pouvoir, de clôture, de classification.

content:

author: Daron Letts
title: Critical thinking goes viral with online media literacy program
content:
Truth could be a money-maker for young people across Nunavut and Nunavik who join the third annual Teen Fact-Checking Network, an online educational initiative by Ottawa-based MediaSmarts.


Under the paid program, participants aged 13 to 19 receive training in verifying information that circulates on the internet.


“We think this would be a valuable opportunity for Inuit youth to build digital literacy and fact-checking skills while also exploring and challenging misinformation related to Inuit culture, communities and issues,” said MediaSmarts spokesperson Tricia Grant, in an email.


Teens stand to earn $150 for analyzing one viral claim bouncing around social media. After that, MediaSmarts pays $100 per fact-check.


The nonprofit charitable organization, founded in 1996, introduces youth to critical thinking skills, reverse image searching and other digital strategies before letting them loose to investigate claims on their own feeds, Grant said

.


Once a participant confirms the content as true or false, they present their research in videos that are then shared on MediaSmarts’ TikTok, Instagram and YouTube channels.


The hope is these videos will help others understand how to assess the authenticity of the content that pops up on their social media feeds, Grant said.


MediaSmarts is looking to partner with Inuit organizations, schools and community groups in Nunavut and Nunavik, and has already connected with

Iqaluit’s Ampere educational hub.


“We’re definitely going to be telling our students to go check this out,” said Kent Driscoll, Ampere’s director of advocacy and strategic initiatives.


The fact-checking project dovetails nicely with Ampere’s weekly film and television production class, he said.


“Inevitably when you’re doing film and television production with youth now, the videos become something online,” he said. “The Teen Fact-Checking Network definitely helps us help our learners better navigate that space.”


Toronto-based United for Literacy, which plans to have math and literacy tutors in 12 of Nunavik’s 14 communities from October till June, is collaborating with MediaSmarts on a national forum in October.


“Literacy leads to critical thinking and if MediaSmarts is offering opportunities for children and youth of all communities, including Nunavik and the North, to be part of initiatives where they can develop their critical thinking skills and improve their digital media literacy, I think it’s always a good thing,” said Mélanie Valcin, CEO of United for Literacy.


Over the past two years, 25 teen fact-checkers involved in the program have scrutinized claims about health, science, the environment, and beauty products, generating more than 7.5 million views across MediaSmarts’ social media channels.


Applications are accepted until Sept. 28 on the MediaSmarts website.

title: Firefighter, EMT, Stuyvesant High School Student Describe 9/11 Exposure & Long Fight for Healthcare
content:
Twenty-five years after the 9/11 attacks, many New York City residents are still grappling with complicated health conditions related to exposure to the toxic air and debris around ground zero.


“We were digging through the pile and using rakes to spread out all the debris to look for anyone’s remains,” says retired New York City firefighter Brenda Berkman. “We were working alongside really heavy equipment, as time went on, that picked up big loads of debris and dumped it, creating a cloud. This went on for 10 months. And at first, there was no proper decontamination at all.”


“

EMS

 personnel were told, 'Oh, you couldn't be getting sick. You’re not a firefighter. So don’t worry. Just go back to work,’” says retired New York City

EMT

 Marianne Pizzitola. “Moving into the years right after, … we started to find consistent diagnoses at our retiree meetings.”


Author and public health advocate Lila Nordstrom recounts how students at her school, Stuyvesant High School, located just three blocks away from ground zero, were also misled by officials after the attacks.

title: Özgür Çelik: Savcılık odalarını seçim odalarına çevirdiniz
content:
Üsküdar Belediyesi’nde 5 Eylül’de salt çoğunluk sağlanamadığı için ertelenen başkanvekili seçimi bugün yeniden yapıldı. Dört tur süren seçim sonucunda AKP’nin adayı Dündar Ziya Gültekin 23 oyla başkanvekili seçildi. CHP’nin adayı Sibel Tan Çetinkaya ise 19 oy aldı.


Seçimin ardından YENİ Parti İstanbul İl Başkanı Özgür Çelik, belediye binası önünde açıklama yaptı. Çelik, seçim sürecinde CHP’li meclis üyelerine yönelik gözaltı ve tutuklamalar ile bazı meclis üyelerinin AKP’ye geçmesine ilişkin çeşitli iddialar ortaya attı.


Çelik, “Sekiz meclis üyemiz Kartal Adliyesi’ne davet edildi, savcılar meclis üyelerimizi yargı tacizi altına aldılar. Yetmedi, iki meclis üyemiz sırf oy kullanamasınlar diye tutuklandılar. Üyelerimiz transfer edildi, bir siyasi parti rozeti takıldı” dedi.


‘Adalet Bakanlığı oğlunu Türkiye’ye getirme sözü verdi’


Meclis üyesi Ahmet Baybaşdar hakkında konuşan Çelik, Baybaşdar’ın ilk seçim sırasında kendisine CHP’li Sibel Çetinkaya’ya oy vermesi yönünde verilen sözlere ilişkin bir açıklama yaptığını ileri sürdü.


Çelik, Baybaşdar’ın sözlerini şöyle aktardı:


“Ben AKP’ye oy verdim, tekrar vereceğim. Çünkü terör örgütünden benim oğlum ceza aldı, 15 yıldır Türkiye’ye gelemiyor. Adalet Bakanlığı, benim terör örgütünden ceza almış oğlumu Türkiye’ye getirme sözü verdi.”


Çelik, “AKP ve yargı kolları, Üsküdar Belediye seçimlerinde bir kişi ona oy versin diye üyemizin 15 yıldır Türkiye’ye gelemeyen oğlunu Türkiye’ye getirme sözü verdi” iddiasında bulundu.


Hüseyin Kazan için ‘şartlı tahliye’ iddiası


Çelik, CHP’den AKP’ye geçen bir diğer meclis üyesi Hüseyin Kazan hakkında da iddialar bulunduğunu söyledi.


“Burada Üsküdar’da iddialar var” diyen Çelik, “Diyorlar ki Hüseyin Kazan’ın oğlu, birinci seçimden kısa bir süre önce bulunduğu cezaevi önünden şartlı tahliye edildi” ifadelerini kullandı.


Ayhan Aydın: ‘Savcı beni tutuklanmayla tehdit etti’


Çelik, CHP’den istifa ederek AKP’ye katılan Ayhan Aydın’a ilişkin de şöyle konuştu:


“Ben ve milletvekilimiz, kendisi rozeti taktıktan sonra kendisine hapishane görüşmeleri verildi. Kendisi ağlayarak, benim de milletvekilimizin de duyacağı şekilde, ‘Savcı beni tutuklanmayla tehdit etti. Benim eşim ve oğlum engelli. Bunlara kim bakacak? Bunlara kim bakacak? Engelli eşim ve oğlum var. Ben tutuklanırsam onlara bakacak kimse yok’ diye hüngür hüngür ağladı.”


Çelik, ardından şu ifadeleri kullandı:


“Burada bu uygulamayı gerçekleştirenlere sesleniyorum: Siz engelli çocuğu olan bir insanı teslim aldınız. Siz insanlık onurunu ayaklar altına aldınız.”


‘Tahsin Usta para ve makam teklifiyle teslim oldu’ iddiası


Tahsin Usta’ya ilişkin de çeşitli iddialar bulunduğunu söyleyen Çelik, “Bir milyon diye iddia edenler var, para ile makam teklifi ile teslim olduğunu söyleyenler var” dedi.


Çelik, sözlerini şöyle sürdürdü:


“Bu insanlar teslim olduktan sonra birinin karısı Afrika’dan geldi, ‘Yapma’ diye... Bu insanlara ulaşmaya çalışıldı. Bu insanların başlarına polis bekletildi, şehir dışında bir otel odasında tutuldu. Böyle bir şey olur mu? Hepimizin canını, malını korumakla görevli polisler bu işe alet edilir mi? Bu ifadeler, Sayın Suat Özçağdaş’ın duyduğu ifadelerdir.”


‘İki meclis üyesi daha gözaltına alındı’


Çelik, seçim günü iki meclis üyesinin daha gözaltına alındığını belirterek, “Üsküdar halkının iradesine çöktü” dedi.


Gözaltına alınanlardan birinin Onur Bayav olduğunu söyleyen Çelik, diğer kişinin kimliğinin henüz tespit edilmediğini belirtti. Çelik ayrıca, “Onur Bayav’ın patronunun da savcılığa çağrıldığı, tehdit edildiği şu anda Üsküdar Belediyesi içinde konuşuluyor” iddiasında bulundu.


‘Valilik binayı demir ablukalarla kapattı’


İstanbul Valiliği’nin seçim öncesinde belediye binası çevresinde aldığı güvenlik önlemlerini de eleştiren Çelik, belediye başkanlarının binaya alınmadığını, yalnızca milletvekillerinin içeri girebildiğini söyledi.


Çelik, “Valilik birinci seçimi erken saate koydu. İkinci seçimi yangından mal kaçırır gibi yapmak için elinden geleni yaptı” dedi.


YENİ Parti’nin belediye binasına girebilmek için grup kurduğunu ve dilekçe verdiğini anlatan Çelik, valiliğin daha sonra hiçbir siyasi parti temsilcisinin binaya alınmayacağı yönünde yeni bir yazı yayımladığını söyledi.


‘Savcılık odalarını seçim odalarına çevirdiniz’


Kartal Adliyesi’nde görev yapan savcılara da seslenen Çelik, şöyle konuştu:

title: Mitsubishi inşaatında ölen işçilerin davasının 6’ıncı duruşması görüldü: Ailelerden bilirkişi raporuna tepki
content:
Manisa — Manisa Organize Sanayi Bölgesi’nin 4’üncü kısmında bulunan Mitsubishi Yeni Isı Pompa Fabrikası inşaatında, 2 Şubat 2024’te işçiler Ali Baba Gökalp ile Zülfü Yıldız’ın yaşamını yitirdiği iş cinayetine ilişkin davanın 6’ncı duruşması Manisa 4. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesinde görüldü.

Bir önceki celsede hazırlanan bilirkişi raporunun incelenmesinin ardından bu duruşmada rapora ilişkin tarafların beyanları dile getirildi. Gökalp ve Yıldız aileleri raporun işçileri tali kusurlu gösterme çabasına tepki gösterirdi.

Avukat Özgür Metin, “Raporda müteveffa işçilerin tali kusurlu bulunması kabul edilemezdir. Ülke genelinde iş kazası ve işçi cinayetleri davalarında raporların bu yönlü hazırlanması maalesef alışkanlık haline getirilmiştir. Mitsubishi başta olmak üzere alt taşeron firmalar ve sorumlu yöneticileri yargılanmalı, sürece dahil edilmelidir. Bu işçi cinayetinde sorumlu olan herkes yargılanmalıdır” diye konuştu.

Duruşmada yeni bir bilirkişi raporu olup olmayacağı yönünde celse arasında karar verileceği ifade edilirken bir sonraki duruşma tarihi 10 Kasım olarak belirlendi.

author: Unknown
title: Hürmüz Diril davasında savcı ceza istedi
content:
Şırnak – Beytüşşebap ilçesine bağlı Mehrî köyünde 11 Ocak 2020 tarihinde Hürmüz Diril (71) ve Şimoni Diril (65) çifti şüpheli bir şekilde kayboldu. Şimoni Diril’in cenazesi günler sonra derede bulunurken, Hürmüz Diril’in akıbeti ise hala bilinmiyor.

Olaya dair Apro Diril, Behçet Öztunç ve İsmail Yıldız’ın “kasten öldürme" suçundan yargılandığı davanın dördüncü duruşması Şırnak 1’inci Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi’nde görüldü. Tutuklu fail Apro Diril’in hazır edildiği duruşmaya, tutuksuz yargılanan Behçet Öztunç ve İsmail Yıldız Ses ve Görüntü Bilişim Sistemi (SEGBİS) ile bağlandı. Birçok kişinin takip ettiği duruşma kimlik tespitiyle başladı.

Duruşmada ilk olarak Diril çiftçinin kızı Gülcan Diril, söz alarak "7 yıldır acı çekiyoruz. Teknoloji ve istihbarata rağmen katiller bulunamadı. Tutuklu sanık bu cinayeti işledi ama tek başına yapmadı. Delilleri kendimiz topladık. Sadece adalet istiyoruz. Artık sabrımız kalmadı. Sizden isteğimiz babamızın bulunması ve faillerin cezalandırılmasıdır” diye belirtti.

Daha sonra Diril ailesinin avukatı Rojhat Dilsiz, yaptığı savunmada "Daha önce taleplerden bulunduk, heyet ret etti bu talepleri tekrar ediyoruz. Dosyada yer alan ve sanık ile konuştuğu belirtilen başkası adına kayıtlı ancak Sabri Bulut'un kullandığı belirtilen bir telefon kaydı var. Sabri Bulut'un dinlenmesini istiyoruz. Apro Diril'in telefon kayıtlarının yer aldığı bir kaydın tarafınıza verilmesini talep ediyoruz" ifadelerini kullandı.

Dosya savcısı esas hakkında mütalaasını mahkemeye sunarak Apro Diril'in cezalandırılması ve tutukluluğunun devamını talep etti. Sanık Apro Diril’in avukatı mütalaaya karşı savunma yapmak için ek süre talebinde bulundu. Mahkeme heyeti, failin tutukluluk halinin devamına karar vererek bir sonraki duruşmayı 16 Eylül’e erteledi.

11 Ocak 2020 tarihinde Hürmüz Diril (71) ve Şimoni Diril (65) çifti kayboldu. Şimoni Diril'in cansız bedeni 70 gün sonra evlerinin bin 500 metre kuzey batısında Hêzil Çayı’nda bulundu. Ancak Hürmüz Diril’in akıbeti bu zamana kadar öğrenilemedi.

Şimoni Diril’in ölümüne dair Apro Diril, Behçet Öztunç ve İsmail Yıldız hakkında “Canavarca hisle veya eziyet çektirerek öldürme” ve “Tasarlayarak öldürme” suçundan dava açıldı. Mahkeme 21 Temmuz 2023 tarihinde Apro Diril hakkında, “Canavarca hisle veya eziyet çektirerek öldürme” ve “Tasarlayarak öldürme” suçundan müebbet hapis cezası, Behçet Öztunç ve İsmail Yıldız hakkında ise beraat kararı verdi.

Savcılık 6 yıl 6 aydır haber alınamayan Hurmüz Diril için ayrı bir iddianame hazırladı. İddianamede Apro Diril, Behçet Öztunç ve İsmail Yıldız “kasten öldürme” suçlaması ile şüpheli olarak yer aldı.

content:

Um langjährige Missstände wie niedrige Löhne und Lohndiebstahl zu beseitigen, gründeten die Beschäftigten im Sucat-Lager von DHL Supply Chain in Muntinlupa eine Gewerkschaft und gewannen am 29. Mai 2026 die Wahl zur Anerkennung der Gewerkschaft. Anstatt mit der Gewerkschaft zu verhandeln, kündigte die Geschäftsleitung die Schließung des Lagers an und begründete dies damit, dass der Vertrag mit der Supermarktkette nicht verlängert worden sei. Hochschulbeschäftigte wollen erneut gegen ausbleibende Finanzierung der Universitäten und niedrige Gehälter streiken


Gegen die spalterische und erpresserische Politik der Regierung, für bessere Bedingungen an Universitäten: Mit einem zweiten, landesweiten Streik innerhalb nur einer Woche wollen Hochschullehrkräfte den Universitätsbetrieb in Argentinien an diesem Dienstag landesweit zum Erliegen bringen. Ihre Forderungen sind konkret: Sie verlangen eine Erhöhung der Gehälter um 31,2 Prozent, zuzüglich der Inflationsrate vom August, und außerdem von der Regierung, die Betriebskosten aller akademischen Einrichtungen sicherzustellen – wozu sie eigentlich gesetzmäßig verpflichtet ist.


Schon am vergangenen Mittwoch waren die Hörsäle der Universitäten in Argentinien für 24 Stunden leer geblieben. Das Gewerkschaftsbündnis der Föderation der Hochschullehrenden (FEDUN) und der Föderation der Nationalen Universitätsbeschäftigten (FATUN) hatte den ersten Teil ihres Aktionsplans in Angriff genommen, nachdem die Lohnverhandlungen mit der Regierung erwartbar gescheitert waren. Doch nach drei Monaten platzte den Lehrenden schließlich der Kragen, als die Regierung eine Erhöhung der Gehälter um drei Prozent auf den Tisch legte.


Denn seit mehr als 300 Tagen ignoriert die Regierung das Gesetz zur Finanzierung der Universitäten, das ihr die Erhöhung der Dozentengehälter um 51 Prozent und eine Budgeterhöhung in Höhe von 0,36 Prozent des BIP vorschreibt. Das Gesetz war im vergangenen Jahr nur aufgrund des starken öffentlichen Drucks verabschiedet worden. Weiterhin weigert sie sich, den legislativen Rückschlag für ihren Kurs zu akzeptieren, obwohl sie bislang mit allen Einsprüchen und bereits vier juristischen Anfechtungen gescheitert ist. title: This month people have been tearing Flock cameras off their poles. Perched above public streets,…
content:
baybelletrist

:

Americans Are Cutting Down Flock Cameras. The Company Calls Them Terrorists.

This month people have been tearing Flock cameras off their poles. Perched above public streets, they are birdlike things, weatherproof, and they photograph every passing car and file it in a searchable national database.

Somebody cut two of them in half at Washington Avenue and Westcott in Houston, spray-painted the wreckage, and left an American flag on one of them. Police were notified on the morning of the Fourth of July.

Somebody severed a camera in Rutherfordton, North Carolina. The police department posted the photograph itself and collected more than twenty thousand comments. “Not all heroes wear capes.” “Give them a medal.”

Here is what the cameras do when nobody cuts them down. Cops use them to hunt immigrants and to follow ICE targets across state lines and to find women who ended pregnancies in states where that is a crime and to watch exes and to watch women they want, without a warrant and without a judge. A cop types a reason in a box and the box does not check.

A man in Burleson, Texas, told deputies his girlfriend had taken abortion pills. He showed them the photographs, the FedEx envelope, the instructions. Deputies opened a death investigation into a non-viable fetus, and the district attorney told them the state could not charge her, and they searched anyway: 83,345 cameras across 6,809 networks, a month of everywhere she had been. The reason they typed was

had an abortion, search for female.

 The search reached Illinois and Washington, where what she did was legal. They found her in Dallas.

She came into the sheriff’s office a week later, and they thought she had come to explain the fetus, and she had come to report that the man who called them had put a gun to her head.

A sheriff in Jerome County, Idaho ran his wife’s plate more than seven hundred times in three months. He typed the same reason every time. Test. The attorney general found nothing to charge him with. He retired in April.

The Institute for Justice counts at least twenty-two officers who used the system to track people they were romantically interested in, and calls that almost certainly an undercount.

And the cameras keep falling.

Become ungovernable.

title: Τοποθέτηση ετοιμοπόλεμων αντιπυραυλικών συστημάτων Patriot εντός κατοικημένης περιοχής στα Χανιά
content:
ΧΑΝΙΑ – ΑΝΤΑΠΟΚΡΙΣΗ


Μας στάλθηκε φωτογραφικό υλικό από οικόπεδο στην περιοχή Λειβάδια των Χανίων, ανάμεσα στο περιαστικό δάσος του Αγίου Ματθαίου και το Μ.Α.Ι.Χ. Το συγκεκριμένο οικόπεδο φαίνεται να ανήκει στον ελληνικό στρατό, και εντός του βρίσκονται τοποθετημένες 3 συστοιχίες του αντιπυραυλικού συστήματος Patriot. Και οι 3 συστοιχίες έχουν τοποθετηθεί ώστε να είναι προσανατολισμένες προς τη βάση του ΝΑΤΟ (και δεν έχουν αποθηκευτεί απλώς).


Το συγκεκριμένο οικόπεδο βρίσκεται εντός κατοικημένης περιοχής, λίγα χιλιόμετρα μακριά από τη νατοϊκή βάση. Η παρούσα δημοσίευση τεκμηριώνει πως τα υλικά του πολέμου είναι ήδη τοποθετημένα στις πόλεις, στις περιοχές, στις γειτονιές μας. Τέτοια οπλικά συστήματα θα είναι τα πρώτα που θα εμπλακούν σε ενδεχόμενο κλιμάκωσης, και βέβαια, θα αποτελέσουν και αυτά (εκτός από τη βάση του ΝΑΤΟ), υποψήφιους στόχους.


Τα Patriot έχουν τοποθετηθεί εκεί από τον Μάρτη, όταν ξεκίνησε επίσημα ο πόλεμος στο Ιράν, και έκτοτε δεν έχουν μετακινηθεί. Οι φωτογραφίες έχουν ληφθεί στα τέλη του Ιούλη, αποδεικνύοντας την παρουσία αυτών των συστημάτων πολύ νωρίτερα από τον πρόσφατο επικοινωνιακό ντόρο περί μεταφοράς Patriot από την Κάρπαθο στη Σούδα, μετά την “αποκάλυψη” από δυτικά media ότι το Ιράν σχεδίαζε επιθέσεις σε ευρωπαϊκά εδάφη.


Την κρίση του καπιταλισμού τη χειρίζονται πολεμικά. Η εικόνα των Patriot μέσα σε κατοικημένη ζώνη έρχεται να συμπληρώσει μια συνθήκη που χαρακτηρίζεται από την ακρίβεια για την κάλυψη των καθημερινών αναγκών, την αστυνομική βία που οδήγησε στον θάνατο τον Κώστα Μανιουδάκη (01/09/2023) και τον Ασράφ (26/08/2026), το δηλητήριο του φασισμού, τη δολοφονική “μεταναστευτική πολιτική” στις συνοριακές γραμμές θανάτου, τα ενεργειακά mega-project και τα καρτέλ της ανάπτυξης, που προσδένουν το νησί στο γενοκτονικό καθεστώς του Ισραήλ.

title: Yıldız: Peace comes when people have a say in their own cities
content:
Former Mardin (Mêrdîn) Metropolitan Municipality Deputy Secretary-General Mustafa Yıldız said the Democratic Society and Peace Process should not be confined to high-level political and legal negotiations, but must be built from the local level through people’s participation in decision-making in the places where they live. Yıldız stressed that strong local democracy, participatory budgeting, multilingual public services, the preservation of cultural memory and guarantees for the will of elected local representatives should be among the key priorities of the new period.


Assessing the legal dimension of the Democratic Society and Peace Process, Yıldız said legislation aimed at ending more than 40 years of conflict represented a historic threshold for Turkey. He said the law contained important provisions concerning the laying down of arms, political prisoners and the legal status of members of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK), but added that a comprehensive framework for a political and democratic solution to the Kurdish question had yet to be established.


Yıldız continued: “In my view, this law represents a historic threshold for Turkey. Ending a conflict that has lasted for more than 40 years means taking what has happened out of the realm of security policy and making it the subject of a legal framework adopted by the Grand National Assembly of Turkey (TBMM). The law introduces important provisions concerning the laying down of arms, political prisoners and the legal status of PKK members, but it does not address the political and democratic solution to the Kurdish question with the same clarity. In other words, there is a legal framework for ending the conflict, but a broader democratisation framework addressing how the political problems that gave rise to the conflict will be resolved is not yet strong enough. We all know that the Kurdish question, which has persisted for decades, will not be resolved by this law alone. This law is the first milestone on the road to peace. It has also opened a door.”


Yıldız said the law could not be expected to resolve every aspect of the Kurdish question at once, adding that criticism over the absence of issues such as education in the mother tongue and local democracy should also be considered in this context. Yıldız also said: “Some criticisms say that there is nothing in the law concerning demands for education in the mother tongue, local democracy or similar issues. After 100 years of policies of denial, a specific law concerning the Kurdish political movement has been passed by parliament. The priority was already to silence the guns. The law has opened a door. The rest will be achieved through the political struggle to be waged in this country. I see this law not as ‘peace itself’, but as an important, albeit incomplete, legal threshold in the transition towards peace.”


Laying down arms ends conflict, it does not build peace


Yıldız said a distinction must be made between ending the conflict and achieving lasting peace, stressing that peace cannot be secured simply by silencing the guns: “Laying down arms means the end of the conflict, but it does not mean that peace has been built. Peace is not achieved on the day the guns fall silent; it is achieved when people feel that they are equal citizens. Ultimately, the 2026 Framework Law should not be underestimated; it is genuinely a historic step. But it would also be a serious mistake to see it as meaning that ‘the Kurdish question has been resolved’. The real test will be the democratic and legal reforms that follow this law.”


Local government is not simply about expanding municipal powers


Yıldız said the concept of local government needed to be reconsidered if the new process was to be built from the local level, stressing that the debate should not be reduced simply to expanding the powers of municipalities: “I do not think we should understand ‘local government’ here simply as increasing the powers of municipalities. If the objective really is to ‘build the Democratic Society and Peace Process from the local level’, the issue is much broader than transferring some powers from the state to municipalities. For the Kurds, a possible model could combine strong local democracy, administrative autonomy, participatory governance and fiscal decentralisation within a unitary state.”


Yıldız stressed that the centralised model of governance needed to change and that decisions should be taken as close as possible to …

title: Güleryüz: The time has come for Mr. Öcalan to convey his own message to society
content:
Mahfuz Güleryüz, Deputy Co-Chair responsible for the Central Organization Commission of the DEM Party, spoke to ANF about Abdullah Öcalan’s status, as well as his role and mission in the process.


The process began with the will expressed by Öcalan


Güleryüz stated that the process began with the will expressed by Leader Apo and said that both the state and public opinion are aware of this. Güleryüz said there is a mechanism within the state that tends not to formalize Leader Apo’s role, and noted that four commissions have been established as part of the process, one of which will include Mr. Öcalan.


Güleryüz said: “The beginning of this process essentially took place with Mr. Öcalan. The whole of society and public opinion know the will that President Öcalan has expressed. State institutions and state officials know it as well. However, we are aware that, particularly within the state, there is a mechanism that tends not to formalize Mr. Öcalan’s role.


At the same time, a commission was established through the subcommissions that were created. Alongside this commission, other commissions were also established to follow the process in some way, facilitate its development, and meet its practical needs. Four commissions were established. One of these is the commission in which Mr. Öcalan will participate.


Mr. Öcalan will take on his role in these commissions, particularly in the commissions described as the disarmament and strategic commissions, and will fulfill his role and mission.”


The period of speaking on behalf of Öcalan must end


Güleryüz added that discussions conducted by different circles about the Kurdish people’s leader are creating problems for the healthy progress of the process and said that Leader Apo should convey his own message directly to society.


“Everyone in the public should now understand that it is both right and necessary for Mr. Öcalan himself to speak,” Güleryüz said, continuing: “Especially regarding President Öcalan, as you know, there have once again been very extensive debates in the public sphere recently. Yes, this is a major handicap. It is as though a minefield has been created. Now everyone is speaking on his behalf. Journalists are singing different tunes, politicians are singing different tunes. Everyone is coming up with their own definition of Öcalan. They are making statements based on his words.


Let us put an end to this debate now, and end it as soon as possible. One of the requirements for living and working freely is precisely this. Why should I speak on behalf of Mr. Öcalan, or why should someone else interpret him according to their own understanding? Mr. Öcalan is the most important actor in this process, and perhaps will be one of its principal drivers. Therefore, the time has come—and has already passed—for him to convey his own message to society himself.”


Öcalan’s role in coordinating the process is important 


Güleryüz added that Öcalan’s role in coordinating the process and during the disarmament phase is important. He said that the process has not yet reached the stage of physical freedom, but that the conduct of the process will be addressed together with Öcalan.


Güleryüz said: “We know that the coordination of this process, the conduct of the process, the proper implementation of the disarmament phase, and the discussion of who will be positioned where will be carried out together with Mr. Öcalan. This is important; it is a historic stage.”


The commission is the first concrete step on the Kurdish question


Güleryüz stated that although the commissions established have shortcomings in terms of resolving the Kurdish question, they nevertheless constitute a concrete step, and said that the work of the commissions should not be delayed because of ongoing debates.


Güleryüz said; “Mr. Öcalan himself described this as ‘the first step of a thousand-kilometer journey.’ Therefore, we have always said the following: Yes, the commission is insufficient. It has many shortcomings. That is true. But it is the most concrete step taken toward resolving the Kurdish question, and it is a first in the history of Turkey.”


The Kurdish question is not just about disarmament

title: Mezzadra: Öcalan’s ideas are an integral part of the new internationalism
content:
In the second part of our interview with Italian philosopher and professor of political theory Sandro Mezzadra, we discussed a range of topics, from the destruction and consequences caused by the “War Regime” in Afghanistan, particularly the 2014 Shengal Genocide attack by ISIS, to the wars escalated across the Greater Middle East and the genocidal policies inflicted upon the Palestinian people.


Mezzadra drew attention to the international interest generated by the democratic, ecological, and women’s liberationist politics developed by Kurdish people’s leader Abdullah Öcalan, and to what this politics can teach peoples engaged in struggles of resistance and progressive circles.


The first part of the interview can be read

here

. 


On August 3, 2014, ISIS carried out a genocidal attack against the Yazidi Kurds in Shengal; it massacred thousands, abducted and sold women, and the fate of thousands more is still unknown. Beyond some states recognizing this as genocide, it did not enter the left's agenda. Why?


I remember writing an article in late summer 2014, when Kobane was under siege. And I mentioned quite emphatically the attack on the Yazidi Kurds in Sinjar. That article was translated into several languages; it was one of myriad statements by scholars, activists, and political organizations and modestly contributed to a significant internationalist mobilization in solidarity with the Kurdish movement and Rojava.


You know better than I do that it was a significant mobilization, including demonstrations in Europe and elsewhere, international delegations to Rojava, and even the participation of internationalist fighters in the Kurdish armed resistance. The Kurdish struggle and Rojava came to figure prominently on the agenda of the global left – or at least a part of it. But I come back to a point I made earlier. Allow me to put it personally: when I wrote that article, I was not speaking “for the Kurds,” nor was I expressing an abstract solidarity. I felt compelled to write and to take action on the basis of a relatively long-standing relationship with the Kurdish movement. And this is, of course, not merely a personal circumstance.


It was the dense web of international relations, exchanges, and networks established around the Kurdish question that made solidarity campaigns with Kobane and Rojava possible. We can discuss the limits of those campaigns, of course, and you may also say that the fate of the Yazidis in Shengal was often subsumed under the broader question of solidarity with Rojava. But for me, the relevance of political relations and infrastructures built over time constitutes a key point of method for internationalism.


Similarly, the war regime withdrew from Afghanistan and left the country to the Taliban regime. There is a terrible situation, especially for women. Whose responsibility is solidarity with the Afghan people?


I feel a certain unease about speaking of “responsibility” for solidarity, since this may suggest that solidarity can simply be assigned to a particular actor. I am perfectly aware that speaking of a new internationalism implies confronting a myriad of situations that put the effectiveness of internationalist practices to the test. Afghanistan is one of those situations, and I am acutely aware of the terrible situation in that country, especially for women.


The fact that the US withdrew from Afghanistan after twenty years of war is an instance of the obstacles and limits encountered by the most powerful war machine in history – of its inability to win a war. Acknowledging the responsibility of the US for the current situation in Afghanistan does not in any way obscure the brutality and the reactionary character of the Taliban. At the same time, the situation we now have in the country is a kind of prolongation of the war regime, meaning that there is neither war nor peace. In such a situation, there are people working on the ground to provide assistance and solidarity to the Afghan people.


I think for instance of the NGO Emergency, which runs three surgical centres, a maternity centre, and a network of more than thirty first-aid posts and healthcare centres in the country. You see here how the boundary between humanitarianism and internationalism is blurred. The continuity of such initiatives can play a key role in creating the conditions for broader solidarity campaigns. At the same time, such initiatives are also connected with practices of resistance (even the …

title: Karasu: A process not completed with freedom of Öcalan cannot reach a conclusion
content:
KCK Executive Council (EC) Member Mustafa Karasu answered Medya Haber’s questions about the current agenda. Commenting on the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the framework law passed by Parliament, Abdullah Öcalan’s role in the process, the Kurdish Culture Festival, debates concerning Alevis, and the future of Êzidîs in Şengal, Karasu said that the process cannot be addressed solely under the heading of disarmament.


This is the first part of the interview.


Commemorative events in memory of the martyrs continue to take place throughout Kurdistan and Turkey. The high level of public participation and the interest shown by the general public are particularly striking. What is your take on this?


First of all, I want to gratefully and respectfully commemorate those who pioneered the July 14 Resistance, comrades Kemal, Hayri, Akif, and Ali, as September 7 marks the anniversary of the martyrdom of comrade Kemal. Their martyrdom has a crucial place in the history of Kurdistan. They are symbols of prison resistance. And it was the prison resistance, as a whole, that paved the way for the events leading up to August 15. The philosophy of life and struggle they created has become the philosophy of life and struggle for the Kurdish people’s freedom fighters. This philosophy of life and struggle has carried our struggle for freedom to this day. We will always remember them. We will strive to live up to their memory.


It was the month of September that this tragic incident took place in Amed. In the corridors of the Amed prison – specifically, in the corridors of Diyarbakır Prison No. 5 – ten comrades were brutally murdered. Their heads and bodies were shattered with planks studded with iron nails. I also respectfully remember those comrades. What they had to face and the way that they faced it shows the nature of their resistance and their stance. The state responded to this with a massacre. Our comrades’ heads were shattered. They will never be forgotten. They will always be remembered.


Many memorials for the martyrs are being held these days. The people have shown a very strong sense of ownership. We are once again commemorating all our martyrs with gratitude and respect. The fact that these memorials are taking place during this process, and the very strong sense of ownership shown by the families of the martyrs and our people, essentially reflects a stance and attitude of embracing the process led by Rêber Apo [Kurdish people’s leader Abdullah Öcalan]. It has demonstrated the Kurdish people’s strong ownership of this process. One can say that these memorials for the martyrs have played an important role. Indeed, at all these memorials, both the families of the martyrs and our people now want the martyrs’ struggle to culminate in a peace process – in peace and a democratic solution. They say that this will make these martyrdoms more meaningful. We, too, want to bring the martyrs’ struggle to a conclusion through the Peace and Democratic Society Process by concretizing it on the basis of democratization and the resolution of the Kurdish issue.


When Rêber Apo launched this process, as well as in previous periods, he stated that he turned to this path of resolution to fulfill the memories and aspirations of the martyrs. We want to bring this process to a successful conclusion. We want to bring it to a successful conclusion through the people’s struggle and the people’s ownership of it.


Undoubtedly, this is not a straightforward process. It is not easy – after all, it is the resolution of a centuries-old problem. In this regard, the debates and struggles surrounding this resolution process continue. As we commemorate the martyrs of September and hold memorial services for them, we have also learned today that the esteemed patriotic politician and mayor of Ağrı has passed away due to illness. I extend my condolences to his family and to all the people of Kurdistan.


During this time, the 34th annual Kurdish Culture Festival in Europe also took place. Participation in the festivities was quite large, and reports described the atmosphere as very lively and enthusiastic. Were you able to follow the festivities through the media? If so, we’d like to hear your impressions.


To a certain extent, we were able to follow at least parts of the event. Obviously, participation was higher than last year, and the atmosphere seemed to be much better than last year. After all, this year’s festival was dedicated to the martyrs …

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Arms Firm That Sold Spy Tech to Dictatorships Wins UK Police Data Contracts
content:
A weapons company that sold mass surveillance technology to dictatorships is now helping British police forces manage their data, a

civil liberties group has said

.


BAE Systems Digital Intelligence has signed two government contracts worth £3.6m since December 2025 to support the police with “data integration and exploitation”, documents obtained by Statewatch show.


The contracts are part of a plan to save £354m by making the police more efficient. They will see BAE provide “technical and service designs for integrating data across the policing landscape” and “linking policing data” across different agencies.


The firm, a subsidiary of BAE Systems, previously

sold hi-tech cyber tools

 to governments in Tunisia, Saudi Arabia, Oman and the UAE, which campaigners said enabled them to spy on millions and thwart dissent.


Its sales included decryption software that “could be used against the UK and its allies”, the BBC reported when it broke the story in 2017. The company said at the time that it works “within the regulatory framework of all relevant countries and within our responsible trading principles.”


The recent UK contracts are part of a plan to build a “police data factory” to help police forces share intelligence, Statewatch reported. Privacy campaigners say they are concerned the National Data Integration and Exploitation Service will use AI.


Alamara Khwaja Bettum, Statewatch’s executive director,

 told Computer Weekly

 that any use of AI in the system would “reflect historic and existing biases within these institutions” and could “lead to over-policing and criminalisation of marginalised communities, particularly racialised groups, migrants and people from low-income neighbourhoods.”


The Home Office told Statewatch the BAE contracts would help “release significant productivity benefits in support of local policing” and “meet policy commitments on policing reform”.


A group of UN experts in 2024

called on BAE Systems

 to stop supplying parts for F-35 fighter jets to Israel amid its genocide in Gaza, saying it was at risk of being complicit in “serious violations” of international law.

Mizrakli  7 sal in girtî ye û pênc sal in jî ew û Selahattin Demirtaş bi hev re di heman qawişê de dimînin.


Selçûk Mizrakli di doza “propagandaya rêxistinê”de beraet kiriye


30 Îlon 2021

Piştî ku Mizrakli ji girtîgehê derket parlamenter û rêveberên DEM Partiyê jî di nav de bi girseyeke qelebalix hat pêşwazîkirin. Piştî vê Mizrakli li pêşiya girtîgehê daxuyaniyek da.

Dema ku navê Girtîgeha Edirneyê tê gotin, Demîrtaş tê hişê mirovan. Beriya min divê Demîrtaş bihata berdan û niha li vir bûya.
